original.detail: CI fails deterministically on this PR: test/pipeline-conflicts.test.ts:381 'conflict resolution gets one checked round: gates/audit/review/verify' (all four). The PR report now passes through holdout redaction with observed-literal collection, so ordinary report text is withheld: the review summary 'LGTM: checked the diff against every requirement' becomes '[private detail]: checked the diff ... [1 private details withheld]', and the holdout table rows become '[private detail]'. For GitHub-published copies, withhold holdout-derived literals only (as for model-bound text) and do not collect literals from the value itself, so non-holdout wording such as a review summary survives. Then decide explicitly whether holdout scenario descriptions may appear in the published report (they are holdout text; withholding them is the safer rule) and update those tests to the chosen rule with a comment, keeping them as regressions for the publication guard. Run test/pipeline-conflicts.test.ts and every other pipeline-*.test.ts file before finishing; the PR's own gates timed out during a machine overload and never checked them.

original.title: An unreadable ancestor leaves higher ancestors selectable
original.detail: The ancestry walk in src/util/proc.ts:57 and src/util/processes-darwin.ts:125 stops at an ancestor it can't read, but discovery then continues with the incomplete exclusion set. An unreadable parent can have a readable, marked ancestor (for example a test runner or daemon carrying the invocation marker), which cleanup will select and signal. A probe feeding both real scanners synthetic inspection data (an unreadable parent with a marked grandparent) returned that grandparent as a selected descendant. Fail closed on incomplete ancestry (refuse to select, or skip signalling, when the caller's ancestry can't be established) rather than relying on the partial set, and add a regression for both the Linux and Darwin scanners with an unreadable parent and a marked higher ancestor.

original.title: Cancellation-test failure paths still signal cached, possibly recycled PIDs
original.detail: At test/failure-injection.test.ts:1133 and :1349 the new Set removes pids only after successful settlement and disappearance checks. If settlement rejects after the descendants have exited, the finally block sends SIGKILL to every retained numeric pid without confirming it is still the original process, which is the recycled-id hazard #441 describes. Executing the test body with an injected settlement failure and a fake signal backend recorded two SIGKILL attempts against simulated recycled ids. Make the failure paths ownership-aware too: only signal a pid whose identity (for example start time or the invocation marker) still matches what the test recorded, or drop pids once they are known gone regardless of how settlement ended.

original.title: A resolution that drops the PR's whole change passes the audit and is pushed
original.detail: `allowEmpty: resolution` exempts every conflict-resolution round from the audit's empty-diff rule, including the delivery-time conflict rounds that ordinary runs already use. A resolution that takes the base's version of every conflicted file erases the PR's change, and the factory pushes it. Reproduced in test/conflict-rounds.test.ts: a resolver that writes the base's 'base intent\n' to greeting.txt makes the round succeed and push a merge whose tree equals main. With the exemption removed, the audit blocks it. Required: a resolution whose tree equals the base tip (model-made or a clean merge) ends without pushing, as needs_human with a reason such as 'the resolution leaves no change against <base>'. Don't re-run the implementer for it (the probe spent 2 implement rounds). Flip 'a clean merge with the base's exact tree still goes through audit and review' to expect no push, and add the same case for a delivery-time conflict round.

original.title: The resolution review can't see PR hunks that the resolution dropped
original.detail: The resolution's audit and review see only the change against the new base. A conflicted file resolved to the base's side, or with part of the PR's hunks removed, shows nothing about what the PR lost. Codex reproduced it: the PR edits a file, the base edits it too, and the resolver keeps the base's version; the round succeeded and the audit patch was empty. Required: give the resolution review the conflicted files' diff against the PR head (the merge's first parent) as well as against the base, and ask it to confirm that each of the PR's changes to those files survives. Test: that probe must end needs_human (the review sees the dropped hunk, and the fake reviewer keys off the presence of the first-parent diff) and push nothing.

original.title: Migration rebuilds review_rounds: CI is red, it isn't additive, and rollback numbering collides
original.detail: (a) CI fails on test/feed-store.test.ts 'the additive migration keeps inbox rows…' with 'no such table: main.review_rounds'. After DROP TABLE, ALTER TABLE … RENAME re-validates every trigger, and that test's database has no feed migrations, so stock SQLite reports 'error in trigger feed_review_approved: no such table: main.feed_add'. Apple's system SQLite 3.54.0 passes, which is why it passed locally. Reproduce on macOS with Homebrew SQLite 3.53.4 via a preload that calls Database.setCustomSQLite('/opt/homebrew/opt/sqlite/lib/libsqlite3.dylib'). A fully migrated database does migrate on 3.53.4. (b) AGENTS.md requires additive migrations. (c) Main numbers rounds as count of all rows + 1, and this PR numbers per kind. After a rollback, main inserts review round (all rows + 1); after re-upgrading, the new per-kind count + 1 collides on UNIQUE, which Codex reproduced with main's Store. Required: ALTER TABLE review_rounds ADD COLUMN kind TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'review' with no CHECK (validate in code: CI fix rounds, the next M5.5 item, will add a kind). Drop and recreate only the two feed triggers. Keep UNIQUE(pr_url, round), and number every round of a PR in one sequence (all rows + 1, as main does). The review cap counts kind='review' only, and titles may show a per-kind ordinal. Test: a conflict row, then main's column-list insert at all rows + 1, then a review round from the new code succeeds. Accepted: while rolled back, main counts conflict rounds against the review cap; no separate table is needed.

original.title: Marking delivery overwrites newer approvals and other land entries
original.detail: markRoundDelivered marks every unstale approval of the PR stale, including an approval of the delivered SHA itself. It also rewrites every blocked entry of the PR whose reason matches LIKE 'conflicts with %'. Codex reproduced both: (1) crash after the push but before markRoundDelivered, approve the new head through submitReview, resume, and that approval becomes stale; (2) a newer land entry blocked 'conflicts with main' gets the 'conflict resolved at…' reason. Required: update only the land entry recorded on the round's trigger (conflict_triggers.land_entry_id), and only while it is still blocked with exactly 'conflicts with <its baseBranch>' (compare the string, don't LIKE-match). Mark stale only approvals whose sha differs from the delivered sha. Tests: both scenarios.

original.title: Cached snapshots decide eligibility, and refusals are final
original.detail: processConflictTriggers and startConflictTrigger prefer the cached poller snapshot (githubPrData) to a live lookup, and every refusal is marked 'skipped' for good. Codex reproduced three cases: (1) a land trigger at the current head with an older cached head makes no live lookup and is skipped 'PR head moved' permanently, so the conflict is never resolved; (2) a later poll of the same head, now no longer draft, doesn't recover a trigger skipped as draft; (3) a cached non-draft snapshot started a round on a PR that was a live draft. Required: land and startup triggers verify with a live readPrHead lookup, and that verified observation (not the cache) decides the state, draft, head, branch and fork checks. The poller path may use the fresh snapshot it just took. Skip only on a definitive result. A lookup failure leaves the trigger pending, with a bounded number of attempts after which it is skipped with the error, so every pending trigger ends. Tests: the three scenarios plus the bounded lookup failure.

original.title: A delivered round pushes again after a restart if the branch was reset
original.detail: deliverReviewRound infers an earlier push only from the remote head. If the round's delivered_sha is recorded and someone has since reset the PR branch, a resume pushes again and undoes the reset. This PR adds two gh calls (the comments lookup and the comment) between markRoundDelivered and the delivery-complete checkpoint, which widens that window. Codex reproduced it: kill at the delivery-complete save, reset the PR branch to the original head, resume, and the round pushes again. Required: when the round's delivered_sha is recorded, never push; finish only the remaining steps (comment, checkpoint) or stop. This also fixes review rounds, which share the function. Out of scope here: the other resume finding (HEAD differs from the reviewed SHA at delivery) is pre-existing on main for every delivery path and is tracked as #459. Don't fix it in this PR.

original.title: A CI round and the land queue can act on the same PR at once
original.detail: A CI round can start, and deliver, while a land entry for the PR is active. Delivery then rewrites entries in queued, checking, waiting_ci or merging, and an abort subscription tries to stop the worker. Codex reproduced the race: the land worker is in merging on head H with its merge response pending; CI delivery records D and blocks the entry; the merge response arrives and landed() overwrites the entry with 'landed, merged H'. Meanwhile D was pushed to a PR that merged without it. The overlap is common: when CI fails on the queue's own pushed merge, the classifier emits ci.needs_fix while the entry is still waiting_ci. Required invariant: a PR never has an active land entry (queued, checking, waiting_ci or merging) and a non-terminal CI round at the same time. Enforce it where each record is created, in the same SQLite transaction as the check: (1) Round start: startRoundTrigger for kind ci checks that the PR has no active land entry before inserting the round. If one exists, the trigger stays pending. That check runs from the database before any live gh lookup, waiting does not count against the 5-attempt bound, and a PR that merged meanwhile is skipped. (2) Land request: the queue refuses to create an entry while the PR has a round of any kind in flight. That includes explicit-SHA requests (`limitless land <pr> --sha <head>`), which bypass approval staling. Keep a re-check at the queue's merge step for conflict rounds, which can legitimately start while an entry is active. Using withPrLock is up to you. Remove the abort subscription and the rewriting of active entries. Tests: a ci.needs_fix while the entry is waiting_ci starts no round and makes no gh calls until the queue blocks the entry, then starts exactly one. A land request at the PR head, explicit SHA included, while a CI round is in flight is refused with a clear reason. The held-merge interleaving above can't end with D pushed and the PR merged at H.

original.title: An honest 'stop and report' costs three implementation attempts
original.detail: The CI round tells the implementer to stop and report when a failure is environmental or outside the change's scope (a flaky test unrelated to the PR, for example). Making no change then trips the empty-diff audit, and the loop retries implementation. Codex observed a stop-only response end needs_human only after 3 implementation attempts, each one a paid model call on a failure the PR didn't cause. Of the two CI failures on factory PRs on 2026-10-10, one (#451's) was an unrelated flaky test. Required: in a CI fix round, an implementation that produces no change ends the round needs_human at once, without retrying. The implementer's report, redacted, is the needs_human reason, so a person or agent sees why. Test: a fake implementer that changes nothing ends needs_human after one implement invocation and pushes nothing.

original.title: A client-chosen consumer name lands in requestedBy, which the factory trusts
original.detail: limitless_create_run now stores the MCP consumer name as the run's requestedBy. Elsewhere requestedBy carries an identity the factory acts on: `requestedBy === "dependabot[bot]"` switches on free-first routing (src/pipeline/context.ts:276, freeFirstRouting) and makes review treat the run as a dependency update (src/pipeline/engine.ts:1408, dependencyUpdate). So any MCP client that names its consumer `dependabot[bot]` gets different routing and a dependency-bump review for arbitrary code. Required: keep the client's name out of identity fields. Either store it namespaced (requestedBy = `mcp:<consumer>`, with ownRuns matching that) or record provenance in sourceRef (`{kind: "mcp", consumer}`). In both cases no client-supplied string may equal a value the factory branches on. Test: create_run with consumer `dependabot[bot]` gives a run for which freeFirstRouting is false and the review prompt's dependencyUpdate is false, and ownRuns still finds it.

original.title: An invocation can over-admit and hold leases without bound
original.detail: A caller-controlled `running` flag goes into the semaphore without proof that it recovers an earlier lease, and there's no cap on lease count or total duration. original.title: Cached gate results and stored handles are reused without checking the commit they ran on
original.detail: `runGateExecution` returns `gateResults.values[purpose]`, or attaches the stored `gateExecution.handle`, whenever the stage, round and purpose match. It never compares `gateResults.sha` or `handle.request.headSha` with the checkout's current head. The ordinary gates stage has a `checkedSha` guard on gate evidence, but the rebase gates in `mergeForDelivery` (engine.ts ~2389) have none, and `completeMerge` runs only when head equals `before` (engine.ts:2381), so a resumed delivery accepts whatever merge commit is checked out. Reproduced with a temporary test: an injected executor checked merge M1, the checkout then held M2 with the same parents, and the daemon was killed at the `gate-started` checkpoint, and again at the `gate-result` checkpoint. On resume the run succeeded and published M2 with zero new executions in both cases. With a sha comparison added, both cases refused. Fix: before reusing either a cached result or a stored handle, compare the recorded sha with `headSha(cwd)`. On a mismatch, discard both and run fresh. Slice 2's remote executors depend on the same pin. Test: restart at both checkpoints with the head moved, and assert a new execution happens (or the stage refuses) and the moved commit is never published on the old result.

original.title: A restart during a pending retry replays it without the setup it depends on
original.detail: Retries run with `setup: []` because on main they follow the first attempt in the same checkout, after its setup. After a restart, the gates stage calls `checkoutCommitted` (removing ignored dependencies and build output), `runGateExecution` returns the cached `initial` result (gate-execution.ts:23), and the stored regression-retry handle then replays only the selected checks, with no setup. Reproduced with a real local setup command that creates `node_modules/ready`, and a check that needs it and fails transiently once. Uninterrupted, the retry passes (flaky). Killed at the retry's `gate-started` checkpoint and resumed, the retry fails with `missing-setup`, the check is recorded as regressed and blocking, and the run spends another implementation round. Main re-runs the whole stage, setup included, on resume. Baseline retries have the same exposure after prepare's cleanup. Fix, whichever is smaller: either (a) drop the completed-result cache for local and replay the stage from the start on resume, as main does, discarding a stored handle for a later purpose; or (b) make a replayed retry run the stage's setup before its checks. The second is also what a fresh remote checkout will need. Test: the setup-dependent check above, killed during the retry and resumed, gives the same verdict as uninterrupted.

original.title: Gate hooks reach only the local executor; an injected executor's events are dropped
original.detail: `executeGate` passes `hooks` only into `localExecutor(hooks)`. When `injected` is used (the seam's purpose), `onResult` is never called: that feeds the engine's per-check gate events and the land queue's log (`appendFileSync` in land/queue.ts:397). `onWait` and `holder` are dropped too. `execution.events` is produced by the local executor, but nothing in `executeGate` or its callers iterates it. Production only uses local today, so nothing visible breaks yet, but a second executor would silently lose gate events and land logs. Fix: make `executeGate` the one place that turns execution events into hook calls (setup and check results, so the land log keeps its setup lines), and have the local executor report through its events rather than calling `hooks.onResult` directly, so a result is reported once. Test: inject a fake executor that emits a setup and a check result, and assert the land log contains both lines and the run gets the gate event.

original.title: A slow but answering lease service is still treated as unreachable, so the command runs unslotted
original.detail:
Prompt busy replies now exhaust the wait budget and exit 75 without running the binary, which fixes that part of the earlier finding. Slow replies still fail open, though. `wrapperLeaseClient` falls back to the Unix socket on any HTTP error, including a timeout, and `withGateLease` (src/cli/gate-slot.ts:152) then treats the socket's error as proof that the service is unreachable, because it isn't a `DaemonTimeoutError`. Reproduced with a temporary probe:
- An HTTP service that answers after 1.3 s and an absent socket: the real binary started unslotted after 1.07 s of a 5 s budget. The same service then returned a valid busy reply.
- 13 busy replies, each delayed past the 2 s request timeout: the binary ran unslotted at 31.9 s of a 60 s budget, because `lastReply` only advances on a reply that arrives in time.

The daemon is slowest exactly when the machine is loaded, which is when slotting matters. Fix: keep a timeout's classification through the transport fallback, so a timeout followed by a socket error still counts as a timeout. Count a late reply as proof the service is alive. Run unslotted only when every transport failed to connect, never because a request was slow. Test: with a fake HTTP client that times out and a socket client that throws a connection error, and with replies delayed past the request timeout, assert the binary doesn't start and the wrapper exits 75 at its budget.

original.title: A delayed recovery reply stops heartbeats while the work keeps running
original.detail: Recovery isn't idempotent across a timeout. The service marks the old lease recovered (src/gates/agent-tests.ts:135, :163) before its reply reaches the wrapper. If that reply arrives after the request timeout, the wrapper retries with the old id, gets `LeaseRejected`, and line 182 stops scheduling heartbeats. When the late reply then arrives, `request` adopts the new id, but heartbeats are never restarted. Reproduced with a temporary probe: delay the first recovery reply, advance past the timeout and the rejected retry, then deliver the reply. Occupancy went back to 1, then fell to 0 while the work was still running, and another invocation took the gate lane. Fix: make a retried recovery for the same lease return the same new lease instead of rejecting it (or let the wrapper ask which lease it holds), and make adopting a late recovery keep heartbeats going. Test: the sequence above, asserting occupancy stays 1 until the work ends and no second invocation acquires the lane meanwhile.

original.title: With enforcement on, read routes still serve holdouts, verify results and other runs' data to any loopback caller
original.detail: `protectedRequest` exempts GET and HEAD everywhere except `/api/admin*` and `/mcp`. Codex editors keep loopback network (no port deny), and an implementer can read its own run id from its worktree path or branch name. Measured against the running release on main: `GET /api/runs/<id>/artifacts/holdout-scenarios.json` returns 200 with the hidden scenarios. A temporary probe at this head, with `require_api_token = true`, got 200 and seeded content without credentials for `holdout-scenarios.json`, `verify-1.json` and run detail including the prompt. All three SSE routes (`/api/stream`, `/api/runs/:id/stream`, `/api/chat/:id/stream`) also returned 200. Run lists and detail, events, artifacts, chat and feed expose other runs' data as well, and holdouts are what keeps verification blind. The issue leaves only `GET /api/health` open. Fix: when enforcement is on, every route needs the token or a session, except `/api/health`, the sign-in pages and assets the sign-in page needs, the passkey sign-in endpoints, and the signature-verified `/webhooks/*`. Update the clients that read (setup's `/api/github/access`, `follow()`, MCP reads) and keep the loopback UI usable through sign-in (see the sign-in finding). Test: with enforcement on, a credential-free loopback GET of an artifact, run detail, events and each stream gets 401, and the same requests with the token or a session succeed.

original.title: A loopback caller can claim to be a trusted proxy and skip the token check
original.detail: The token check is skipped when `access === "proxy"`, and `classifyRequest` (src/server/access.ts:27) returns "proxy" for any peer in `trusted_proxies` that sends an `x-forwarded-*` header. When the proxy runs on the same machine (`trusted_proxies = ["127.0.0.1"]`), every loopback process can send those headers. Reproduced with a temporary probe: enforcement on, `trustedProxies = ["127.0.0.1"]`, `auth = "proxy"`, and a spoofed `x-forwarded-for` plus a public Host and Origin. The response was 201 and a run was created with no credentials. With `auth = "required"` the same request got 401. Host and Origin are caller-controlled. Fix: forwarded headers from a loopback peer must never replace the token or session requirement. Either require a configured proxy secret header on proxied requests from loopback, or refuse at config load the combination of enforcement, a loopback trusted proxy and `auth = "proxy"`, with a clear message. Test: the request above gets 401, and a correctly configured proxy still works.

original.title: A failed second start replaces the running daemon's token file

original.title: Short multiline holdout prose written with `\n` escapes still leaks its later lines
original.detail: Real newlines (LF and CRLF) are now covered, along with context lines, renamed content, indentation changes, no-final-newline markers and page boundaries, and so is long prose with JSON escapes. A short phrase with an escaped newline is not. Reproduced through MCP with a temporary test using test/mcp-support.ts fixtures: a holdout detail `Amber sky` + newline + `Violet sea`, written into a changed file as the JSON string "Amber sky\nViolet sea", comes back with `Violet sea` unchanged in both the patch and the report. The literal `n` after the backslash defeats the boundary match, and at ten characters the phrase is below the distinctive-substring fallback (DISTINCTIVE_LENGTH, around lines 209–244). Fix: match against text with escape sequences decoded (`\n`, `\r`, `\t`, `\uXXXX`, as `normalizedLayers` already does for other encodings), and withhold the patch lines a match spans. original.title: Adding every line of a multiline detail as its own pattern blanks large parts of unrelated diffs
original.detail: To catch multiline prose across patch prefixes, the round adds every trimmed line of a multiline detail as a separate redaction pattern, however short or generic. Measured with a temporary probe that replays this round's own source and test changes: holdout lines `}`, `return true;` and `expect(x).toBe(1)` altered 181 of 589 changed non-blank lines (30.7%), plus context lines. `}` alone hit 164 lines, and a function fixture lost 90 of its 120 added non-blank lines. A reviewer can't review a diff that is a third withheld, and the view gives no signal about why. A minimum length alone doesn't help, because `return true;` is generic too. Fix: match multiline details against the hunk's content with the patch prefixes (`+`, `-`, space) stripped, so a phrase is found across lines as written, and withhold exactly the lines a match covers. Then constituent lines don't need to be patterns on their own, except where the line alone is distinctive by the same rule as single-line details. Keep the previous finding's cases withheld. Test: the replayed-diff case above withholds only lines that actually contain the holdout phrase.

original.title: The redaction catalogue is rebuilt from every diagnostic on every page
original.detail: Each `getChange` call re-reads and parses every owner diagnostic of the owner run and all its rounds, then rebuilds both regexes (lines 199–215). original.title: Converting the PR to a draft stops it from landing after approval
original.detail: A blocked round runs `gh pr ready --undo` on a ready PR. original.title: A reset or truncated reply from a live lease service still runs the command unslotted
original.detail: Slow replies now wait and exit 75 at the budget (re-measured: 1.3 s replies with no socket exited 75 at 5.002 s, and 2.5 s busy replies exited 75 at 60.002 s, both without starting the binary). But the unslotted fallback still has no allowlist of connection failures. `withGateLease` treats any first-request error other than `DaemonTimeoutError` or `LeaseRejected` as "unreachable", and `wrapperLeaseClient` (src/cli/agent-test.ts:153) drops the HTTP error when it falls back to the socket. Reproduced with a temporary probe: a live service that resets the connection (`ECONNRESET`) started the real binary unslotted after 39 ms, with a warning, and one that sends truncated response headers did so after 3 ms. (Truncated JSON bodies are correctly rejected without running.) Fix: classify each transport's failure. Fall back to running unslotted only when both transports failed before a connection was made: connection refused, `FailedToOpenSocket`, a missing socket path, and the equivalent codes, as named constants with a test each. A reset, a truncated reply or any other error after connecting means the service is there, so the wrapper keeps waiting within its budget and exits 75. Keep both errors and report them in the warning. Test: the reset and truncated-header services never start the binary and exit 75 at the budget, while refused-on-both still runs with the warning.

original.title: Local gate work can keep running after its execution is forgotten
original.detail: Two paths drop an execution without stopping it. (1) `executeGate` awaits `Promise.all([execution.result, events])`. If a hook called while forwarding events throws (a land-log write, say), the promise rejects, the `finally` neither cancels nor awaits the execution, and `runGateExecution` (gate-execution.ts:62) then clears the handle. Reproduced: a hook threw `log write failed` after the first check, a replacement execution completed, and the original check (`sleep 900`) kept running. (2) gate-execution.ts:29 discards a stored handle for another purpose or SHA with only a save. When that execution is still live in this process, it keeps running too. Normal shutdown cancellation does work, but discarding isn't cancelling. Fix: before forgetting an execution, whether by error, discard or settle, cancel it and await its end. Make a hook failure cancel the execution and surface as the stage's error, so it can't leave a result behind. Test: a throwing hook, and a discarded live handle, each leave no running child (check by the pid the test started) and no occupied gate slot.

original.title: When the catalogue key can't be computed, the final freshness check is skipped and newly private text can be returned
original.detail: On a key failure `key` is null. The catalogue is rebuilt, but the end-of-assembly check that compares the catalogue with current inputs is skipped. Reproduced with a temporary MCP test: the key computation was forced to fail, a verifier diagnostic containing a new private literal (`fallbackRaceSecret`) was appended while Git inspection was in progress, and the response came back `available: true` with that literal unchanged in the report. Fix: when freshness can't be established after the awaits, either rebuild the catalogue and reapply redaction to everything assembled, or refuse with `available: false` ("privacy inputs changed; restart"). Never return content checked against a catalogue that may be stale. Test: the sequence above withholds the literal or refuses.

original.title: A whitespace pattern built from holdout text scans quadratically
original.detail: A multiline detail containing a quoted tab followed by a character (for example `"\tZ"`) yields a pattern with `\s+Z`. Against a long whitespace run ending in a different character, the scan is quadratic: 32K, 64K and 128K characters took 497, 1,670 and 6,293 ms, with 469, 1,633 and 6,251 ms of CPU. That runs before paging, so the page bound doesn't limit it, and both the diff and the holdout text come from untrusted sources. Escaping of metacharacters is fine; this is quadratic scanning, not exponential backtracking. Fix: canonicalize whitespace once (collapse runs to a single space in a normalized copy with a line map) and match details literally against that copy, instead of putting `\s+` in patterns. Test: a 128K whitespace line against such a detail completes in a few milliseconds and the detail is still withheld where it actually occurs.

original.title: The catalogue cache has no size bound
original.detail: The cache helps: with the same fixture (5,000 diagnostics, 10.37 MB), warm reads went from 1,185–1,207 ms to 780–784 ms, and synchronous work before the first await from 378–388 ms to 1 ms. Diagnostic, round, state and privacy-input changes invalidate it correctly. But retention is one catalogue per Store with no cap on bytes or pattern count. original.title: A failed startup leaves started work running and drops the token's protection too early
original.detail: Two cleanup gaps in `startDaemon`. (1) If `mount(factory)` rejects after it has already started the land queue, `integrations` was never assigned, so its `stop()` can't be called. A temporary test injected a failure into real integration mounting after land startup: land started 1, land stopped 0, one notifier timer still live, token protected false. (2) On a real bind failure, `startHttp` (src/server/http.ts:722) releases the token's read protection before `startDaemon` tears down the integrations, so a confined profile built during teardown (a land check still finishing, say) lacks the denial. Fix: make mounting exception-safe, so a partial mount stops what it started (have `mount` clean up after itself on failure, or return its stop handle before the step that can fail). Release the token protection only after every started component has stopped. Test: both injected failures leave no running land queue or timers, and every profile built until teardown completes denies the token path.

original.title: With enforcement on, a proxy-authenticated setup over plain HTTP can never authenticate
original.detail: With enforcement on, proxied requests now need a token or session too (intended: tests and GUIDE say "all routes"). But the HTTPS check on `public_origins` still exempts `auth = "proxy"`, and the session cookie is Secure. Reproduced in Chrome with a temporary test: an HTTP public origin, a non-loopback trusted proxy, `auth = "proxy"` and enforcement on. Password sign-in completed, but the browser kept zero cookies, went back to `/login`, and `/api/runs` returned 401. The config is accepted but unusable. Fix: when `require_api_token` is on, require HTTPS `public_origins` for `auth = "proxy"` as well, with a clear message at config load. Update OPERATIONS, which still says proxy mode has no built-in sign-in, to say that with enforcement on, proxied browsers also sign in to Limitless. Test: the config is refused, and the HTTPS variant signs in and works.

original.title: The gate allowance for the Cargo home exposes Cargo's registry credentials
original.detail: Gates are allowed to read the whole `CARGO_HOME` (default `~/.cargo`), and the credential list (line 89) doesn't include `credentials.toml` or `credentials`, which hold private registry tokens (see Cargo's documented home layout). A temporary probe confirmed that a synthetic `~/.cargo/credentials.toml` falls inside the allowance and has no specific denial. Adding it to `[sandbox] deny_read` instead makes the overlap check (line 122) refuse to launch any gate. Fix: allow only what builds need from the Cargo home (`bin`, `registry`, `git`, `config.toml` and `config`, which `runConfined` already copies into scratch), and deny `credentials.toml` and `credentials` as specific denies that win over the allowance. Do the same review for the bun and rustup homes. Test: a profile and an unconfined real-Seatbelt probe show `credentials.toml` denied while `cargo --version` and a cached registry read work.

original.title: Editors can still read credential stores at relocated paths
original.detail: The credential list uses default paths under the home directory only. `agentEnv()` (src/util/proc.ts:699) passes `CODEX_HOME`, `GH_CONFIG_DIR` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` through, and Codex and gh honour them (gh documents `GH_CONFIG_DIR` and `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`). A temporary probe set synthetic custom Codex and gh homes: `agentEnv()` kept them, and the editor deny list covered neither the custom `auth.json` nor `hosts.yml`. Fix: compute the effective location of each store from the daemon's own environment (`CODEX_HOME`, `GH_CONFIG_DIR`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME/gh`, `LIMITLESS_CONFIG_DIR`, `AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE`, `DOCKER_CONFIG`, `GNUPGHOME`, `KUBECONFIG`, `NETRC`, `NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG`, `CARGO_HOME/credentials*`), and deny those as well as the defaults, in both spellings. Test: with those variables pointing at temporary stand-ins, the editor and gate profiles deny each one.

original.title: Loading another config replaces the running factory's read policy
original.detail: `configureReadPolicy` overwrites a module-global `configured` every time `loadConfig` runs, and `homeReadPolicy` (line 84) reads that global, not the `Config` of the factory that launched the work. Production callers don't set `readPolicyScope`. A temporary probe loaded config A with a custom `deny_read` entry, then config B with no `[sandbox]` table: the next policy dropped both A's entry and A's config-directory denial. Any code path that loads a config in the daemon process (eval settings, `limitless` commands run in-process, tests) can widen a running factory's sandbox. Fix: make the policy part of `Config` (an immutable value built in `loadConfig`), and pass it where profiles are built (through `EngineDeps` or the confinement scope that `executeRun`, the land queue and evals already set), rather than a module global. Test: loading a second config doesn't change the policy that the first factory's gates and editors get.

original.title: Under the new gate profile, this repository's own test suite fails, so every gate would fail after deploy
original.detail: The factory's gates for this PR passed only because gates run the daemon's (main's) profile, not the PR's. Measured on 2026-10-11 by running this PR's `runGates` (the new gate profile) on a recorded worktree of this PR, with the repository cache and checkout under the real home directory as factory checkouts are (`~/.limitless/runs/...`). Setup, lint and typecheck passed, but the test check failed with 6 or more failures. (1) Four UI tests ("original prompt renders plain multiline text...", "Providers keeps controls...", "direct navigation to every UI route...", "guarded UI/assets, API, SSE...") fail with `EPERM: operation not permitted, stat '<home>/package.json'`: Bun's resolver and bundler walk up parent directories looking for package.json (and similarly bunfig.toml, tsconfig.json, node_modules), and with the home-wide read deny the walk gets EPERM instead of ENOENT and aborts. The ancestor `file-read-metadata` grants cover the ancestor directories themselves, not files inside them. (2) Four failure-injection tests ("unconfirmed holdout shutdown preserves its snapshot...", and "an unavailable pinned implementer stops with its chain and reason: disabled|quota|rejected") fail deterministically inside the gate profile (Expected "needs_human", Received "failed", 4 of 4 when run alone under the profile) and pass unconfined in the same checkout. Reproduce with this PR's code: `recordWorktree(wt)`, then `runGates(wt, { setup: [], checks: [{ name: "t", run: "bun test test/failure-injection.test.ts -t 'unavailable pinned implementer'" }] }, signal)`, with `wt` under the home directory. Fix: make what toolchains legitimately probe in ancestor directories resolve as absent or readable (for example allow read of the specific manifest names, package.json, bunfig.toml, tsconfig.json and jsconfig.json, plus metadata for `node_modules` in each ancestor of the allowed roots, never credential paths), find what the failure-injection runs hit under the profile, and add a test that runs a real `bun test` of a small fixture project under the gate profile from a checkout located under a temporary home. Then run the full suite under the new gate profile, from a checkout under the home directory, and report the result in the PR.

original.title: Loading another config replaces the running factory's read policy
original.detail: `configureReadPolicy` overwrites a module-global `configured` every time `loadConfig` runs, and `homeReadPolicy` (line 84) reads that global, not the `Config` of the factory that launched the work. Production callers don't set `readPolicyScope`. A temporary probe loaded config A with a custom `deny_read` entry, then config B with no `[sandbox]` table: the next policy dropped both A's entry and A's config-directory denial. Any code path that loads a config in the daemon process (eval settings, `limitless` commands run in-process, tests) can widen a running factory's sandbox. Fix: make the policy part of `Config` (an immutable value built in `loadConfig`), and pass it where profiles are built (through `EngineDeps` or the confinement scope that `executeRun`, the land queue and evals already set), rather than a module global. Test: loading a second config doesn't change the policy that the first factory's gates and editors get.

original.title: A failed second bind releases token protection before the first listener has stopped
original.detail: Mount failures and a failed first bind now clean up correctly. Re-measured: six injected mount-step failures, profiles built during delayed teardown still deny the token path, repeated `stop()` is harmless, and real CLI SIGINT and SIGTERM shutdown passes. One path remains. When the LAN listener (the second bind) fails, the catch block calls `local.stop(true)` without awaiting it, and `startDaemon` never gets that listener's stop handle. With an injected asynchronous shutdown around a real Bun listener, startup had already returned, token protection was gone, and `/api/health` on the first listener still returned 200. Fix: await both listeners' stop calls in that catch block before releasing (or let the error carry them to `startDaemon`'s `stop`), so protection is released only after every listener has closed. Test: the injected slow-stop case, asserting the listener is closed and the token path still denied until the release.

original.title: Inside a gate, a missing optional toolchain path makes the read policy refuse, so this repository's own suite fails under the new profile
original.detail:
Five of the six earlier findings are fixed: narrow Cargo, rustup and bun allowances with credentials denied, relocated stores denied, a per-config policy, the specific re-deny test, and the two fixtures. The gate-profile blocker is still open. The orchestrator ran this PR's `runGates` on a recorded worktree under the real home, inside `readPolicyScope.run(loadConfig().readPolicy, ...)`. Setup, lint and typecheck passed, and the test check failed after 1,079 s. Every visible failure carried `Cannot resolve read policy path <home>/.rustup/toolchains`:
- "an unavailable pinned implementer stops with its chain and reason: quota|rejected";
- "pinned verifier exhaustion redacts private holdout details: unavailable|rejected";
- "audit allowances > engine audit honors persisted allowances: no opt-in|inline mention";
- "audit allowances > private-string audit events and retry feedback redact filenames and values";
- "a changes verdict runs one round that pushes onto the PR branch with the findings quoted".

This PR's own real-Seatbelt regression, test/sandbox.test.ts:818 "failure-injection outcomes survive a gate checkout under home", also fails unconfined with the same error. Cause: inside a gate, the home directory is read-denied, so the strict component resolver gets EPERM from `realpathSync` (and `lstatSync`) on an absent optional path such as `~/.rustup/toolchains`, instead of ENOENT, and refuses. Tests that build factories and gates run nested inside the gate, so after a deploy every gate of this repository would fail.

Fix:
- Separate required roots (checkout, scratch, Git paths) from optional toolchain candidates (bun, cargo and rustup subpaths, `toolchain_paths`).
- In the component resolver, call `lstatSync(next, { throwIfNoEntry: false })` before `realpathSync(next)`, and don't realpath a component proven absent.
- Treat an optional candidate as absent, and omit it from the allowances, when it doesn't exist, or when its existence can't be inspected because a denied ancestor blocks it (EPERM or EACCES from lstat on a path under the denied home). An optional allowance for a path that can't be seen grants nothing anyway.
- Keep refusing for required roots that can't be resolved, for an existing entry (including a dangling symlink) that can't resolve, and for any overlap with a credential path, even for absent descendants.
- Don't use `existsSync()` or catch-all exception handling to classify absence.

Tests, since real Seatbelt doesn't run in factory gates or CI: make the resolver's `lstatSync` and `realpathSync` injectable, and add non-skipped tests.
- With lstat and realpath throwing EPERM for every path under a temporary home (as inside a confined gate) and no `.rustup`, `.cargo` or `.bun` present, the gate policy computes without throwing and omits those allowances.
- A required root under the same conditions still refuses.
- An existing dangling symlink candidate still refuses.

Keep test/sandbox.test.ts:818 as the real-Seatbelt regression; the orchestrator will run it and the full suite under the profile unconfined.

original.title: Missing-record fallback ignores the configured daemon port
original.detail: Without an `api-token.origin` record (an older daemon), `apiTokenHeaders` authorizes only `http://127.0.0.1:${LIMITLESS_PORT ?? 7400}`. With `[server] port = 7412` in config.toml and no `LIMITLESS_PORT`, setup targets 7412 correctly but sends no authorization header, so authenticated calls to an older daemon fail. The helper would also send the token to port 7400 when that isn't the daemon's port. Measured with a temporary home and a synthetic token. Fix: resolve the effective daemon port the same way the CLI and setup do (the configured `[server] port`, overridden by `LIMITLESS_PORT`). Use one implementation, have every caller pass it, and use it for the fallback origin. Test: no record, configured port 7412, no env → the 7412 origin gets the header, 7400 doesn't.

original.title: After a rollback, newer clients lose access until the stale origin record is removed
original.detail: An older daemon started after a rollback rotates `api-token` but leaves the newer release's `api-token.origin` untouched. On the same listener origin with enforcement enabled, the previous release's CLI got HTTP 200 and this PR's CLI got 401, because the record's `tokenHash` no longer matches. AGENTS.md requires the previous release to keep working across a rollback, and a newer CLI talking to an older daemon is part of that. Fix: treat a record whose hash doesn't match the current token as absent, and fall back to the configured loopback origin (the previous finding). That is exactly the trust an older daemon without a record gets: the record can only narrow the recipient, never widen it. Keep rejecting a record whose origin isn't a plain http(s) origin. Test: a record with a mismatched hash and a token on the configured loopback port → the header goes to that port only.

original.title: A malformed or unreadable config.toml now aborts every CLI and MCP request
original.detail: This round added `loadConfig` calls on client request paths: `src/cli/main.ts:87` (`api()`), the default `localLeaseClient` port in `src/cli/gate-slot.ts:46`, and `httpBackend` in `src/integrations/mcp.ts:216`. They throw when config.toml is mode 000, is invalid TOML, or sets an invalid value such as an unknown `review.mode`. With a malformed config and an explicit `LIMITLESS_URL` pointing at a healthy temporary server, `limitless ls` exited 1 after zero HTTP requests. Lease and MCP client creation threw the same way. On main the CLI didn't load config on these paths, so it kept working against a running daemon. Measured with temporary homes and config dirs. Fix: use one shared, non-throwing resolver for the daemon port (`LIMITLESS_PORT`, else the configured `[server] port`, else 7400) that reads only what it needs and never throws. Use it for the token fallback origin and the default lease port. Keep token handling fail-closed: if the port can't be determined from a readable, valid value, send no token rather than guess a non-default port. Test: with an unreadable config and with invalid TOML, `api()`, the lease client and `httpBackend` still issue their request (without a token unless the default origin matches), and `limitless ls` against an explicit `LIMITLESS_URL` reaches the server.

original.title: The client port resolver disagrees with the daemon, so the token fallback can authorize another listener
original.detail: The daemon resolves its port with `num(Number(process.env.LIMITLESS_PORT) || server.port, 7400)` (src/config.ts:287), so `LIMITLESS_PORT=+49751`, `7413.0`, `1e3` or a hex form all select that number. `resolveClientPort` accepts only `/^\d+$/` and otherwise falls back to `[server] port`. Measured with temporary homes and a synthetic token: with `LIMITLESS_PORT=+49751` and configured port 49752, the daemon used 49751 while the CLI, the lease client and `httpBackend` all chose 49752. With a missing or stale origin record they sent the bearer token to the unrelated listener on 49752, and made zero requests to 49751. Configured port 0 also differs: the daemon binds an ephemeral port, while clients pick 7400. Fix: move the daemon's exact port rule into one small exported function that both `loadConfig` and the client resolver call. It takes the env value and the raw `[server]` table and never throws, so malformed config stays non-fatal. In `apiTokenHeaders`' fallback, send no token unless the resolved port is a definite integer 1–65535 from that same rule; for example port 0, a non-integer, or an unreadable or invalid config with no env override should withhold the token. Keep routing unchanged otherwise. Tests: `LIMITLESS_PORT=+49751` with configured 49752 → client and daemon agree on 49751, and 49752 gets no token; configured port 0 → no token fallback.

original.title: A small caller line cap breaks the confined command's startup handshake
original.detail: `runSandboxed` passes the caller's `maxLineLength` to the line splitter that also parses its 54-character startup marker. Add a test with a cap below the marker length showing the confined command still starts and that long forwarded lines are still truncated.

original.title: The post-merge metadata read opens a window where a cancel is overwritten
original.detail: After `mergePullRequest` succeeds, `merge()` now awaits `(this.deps.client ?? getGitHubPr)(entry.prUrl, signal)` before calling `landed()`. Before this PR, `landed()` ran right after the merge, with nothing awaited in between. A cancel during the new read aborts the signal and records the entry as `cancelled`. The read's `.catch(() => null)` then swallows the abort, and `landed()` → `finish(entry.id, "landed", …)` overwrites the cancel. Late writes must never overwrite a cancel (AGENTS.md, #388). Fix: record the landing exactly as before, immediately after the merge. Then fill `mergedBy` and `mergedAt` as a best-effort, conditional update of the run fields only: it never changes the land entry's state, and it writes only fields that are still null. Add a test that cancels during that read and fails on this PR's current code, and keep the read bounded.

original.title: Marking the owner merged can resolve the landed round as superseded
original.detail: `landed()` now calls `updateRun(id, { merged: true, … })` for both the entry's run and the owner run. `updateRun` calls `supersedeByIssue()` whenever `merged` is set (src/db/store.ts, around line 1780), and that resolves every `needs_human` run in the repository that closes one of the same issues, except the run being updated. The land entry's run is often the review round (for example #514's land entry is its round run), and a round's prompt keeps the original request with its `Closes #N`. So when the round is `needs_human`, the owner update resolves the round that just landed as `superseded`, not merged. Later reconciliation preserves that resolution. Before this PR only the entry's run was updated. Fix: record the merge for each run being landed through the merge resolver (`resolveMergedRun`, which handles needs_human and resolved transitions), before any supersession. Supersession must exclude the runs being landed. Add a test that fails today: a needs_human round and a succeeded owner, both closing #N; after landing, the round is resolved as merged and not superseded.

original.title: Landing publishes before its outer transaction commits, and never drains the feed
original.detail: `landed()` wraps `finish()` and the merge resolvers in a raw `this.store.db.transaction(...)`. That leaves `store.pendingPublications` unset. Each `resolveMergedRun` → `updateRun`/`resolveRun` then opens its own `chatTransaction`, which publishes its run messages as soon as its savepoint returns, while the outer landing transaction is still open (src/db/store.ts, around lines 668-681). Subscribers can therefore see merge and resolution messages that a later failure in the same transaction rolls back. Then `publishFeed()` returns early because `db.inTransaction` is true (around line 686), and nothing drains the feed after the outer commit. So the new `run.merged`, `land.landed` and resolution items wake SSE and long-poll consumers only when some unrelated publication happens. Fix: run the whole landing through one publication-buffered store transaction, for example a store method that reuses `chatTransaction`'s buffering for an outer block. Publish the buffered messages and drain the feed only after the outermost commit. Add a test that subscribes to the store and asserts no run or feed message is delivered before the landing commits, and that the landing's feed items are published right after it.

original.title: Replace the hunk span heuristic with whole-file withholding for multiline private values
original.detail: The run ended after 5 rounds, and its last in-run finding is still open. A credential's last line leaks when a hunk is clipped inside the credential at end of file with no trailing newline. `privatePatchLines` (about 90 lines) reconstructs sides per hunk and matches spans, clipped prefixes and suffixes, and adjacent pairs, and each round has found another hunk-boundary case. Patches are the wrong place to look for a multiline value, because a hunk can show any slice of it. Replace the heuristic with a whole-file check. For the selected file, read its full content at the pinned base and the pinned head with the hardened git wrapper (`git show <sha>:<path>`, with the same literal-path handling already used for the diff). If either side contains any multiline registered credential or multiline private string, return no patch text for that file: `[withheld: private text; 1 file]`. Compare after the same normalization the per-line filter uses (NFKC, lowercase, and CRLF/CR as LF). Otherwise use the existing per-line `privacy()` filter unchanged. Hunk headers, function annotations, clipped hunks and missing trailing newlines then need no special handling, because the file is withheld as a whole. Remove `privatePatchLines`. Keep tests that cover: an added file with a two-line credential; a modified file whose hunk is clipped inside the credential at end of file with no trailing newline (the current failing case); a deleted file containing one; a CRLF variant; and a file with no multiline value whose diff stays fully visible. Each must fail on today's main. Budget: about 40 source lines.

A credential's last line leaks when a hunk is clipped inside the credential at end of file with no trailing newline. `privatePatchLines` (about 90 lines) reconstructs sides per hunk and matches spans, clipped prefixes and suffixes, and adjacent pairs, and each round has found another hunk-boundary case. Patches are the wrong place to look for a multiline value, because a hunk can show any slice of it. Replace the heuristic with a whole-file check. For the selected file, read its full content at the pinned base and the pinned head with the hardened git wrapper (`git show <sha>:<path>`, with the same literal-path handling already used for the diff). If either side contains any multiline registered credential or multiline private string, return no patch text for that file: `[withheld: private text; 1 file]`. Compare after the same normalization the per-line filter uses (NFKC, lowercase, and CRLF/CR as LF). Otherwise use the existing per-line `privacy()` filter unchanged. Hunk headers, function annotations, clipped hunks and missing trailing newlines then need no special handling, because the file is withheld as a whole. Remove `privatePatchLines`. Keep tests that cover: an added file with a two-line credential; a modified file whose hunk is clipped inside the credential at end of file with no trailing newline (the current failing case); a deleted file containing one; a CRLF variant; and a file with no multiline value whose diff stays fully visible. Each must fail on today's main. Budget: about 40 source lines.

original.title: Setup edits to tracked files reach the reviewer
original.detail: After `prepareEvalGates(..., true)` the trial goes straight to the review without restoring tracked files, so the reviewer reads whatever setup wrote instead of the labelled commit. Reproduced with a fixture whose base setup is `printf setup-overwrite > CURRENT.txt`: the readonly reviewer read `setup-overwrite`. Production removes gate-generated edits before review (src/pipeline/engine.ts, the checkout after gates). After setup, restore tracked content to the case head and keep ignored and untracked payloads such as node_modules, then add a test where setup modifies a tracked file and the reviewer still sees the committed content.

original.title: A setup arm counts as production routing evidence and makes policy selection order-dependent
original.detail: Routing evidence counts every single-mode `standard` system with the matching implementer-report mode, and its comment relies on 'at most one such system per target'. `setup: true` makes a second, distinct configuration for the same target, so an eval with a control arm and a setup arm feeds both into policy and the summary picked depends on trial order. Reproduced: control passed, setup arm failed; the selected candidate's pass rate was 1 in one trial order and 0 when the trials were reversed, with zero paired cases in both. Production review doesn't run eval setup, so exclude `setup` systems from routing evidence (the same way non-standard prompts are), with a test that a control plus setup eval routes on the control only.

original.title: A config model that redefines a built-in id now hides a colliding runtime row
original.detail: The guard skips a runtime row whenever its id is any built-in id (`MODELS.some((m) => m.id === model.id)`), whatever the effective model is. The issue keeps a runtime row that collides with an unrelated config model fatal, and treats only a code built-in, or a config model exported from it, as redundant. Reproduced with a throwaway test: config defines `claude/haiku-5.5` with backend `org/unrelated-model`, and a runtime `claude/haiku-5.5` row exists. The PR head starts with the unrelated backend and warns 'redundant runtime entry; using built-in definition', which is false. The merge base throws `catalog collision: claude/haiku-5.5`. Skip only when the existing model is the code built-in, or a config model whose definition equals that built-in's (what `providers export` writes); keep every other collision fatal, and make the warning name the definition actually used. Add a test with a built-in id redefined in config.

original.title: A directory replaced by a file leaks its deleted children's multiline credentials
original.detail: `privateFile` skips a non-blob side (`if (type !== "blob") continue`), but `git diff <base> <head> -- :(literal)<path>` for a path that was a directory at base also prints every deleted child. Those children never get the whole-file check, and their `-` prefixes defeat the per-line filter. Reproduced with a copy of test/mcp-proxy.test.ts: base commits `nest/secret.txt` containing a registered two-line credential, head replaces `nest` with an ordinary file; `limitless_get_change` on `nest` returns the `nest/secret.txt` deletion with both credential lines, on the direct and the proxy backends (Codex also reproduced it for a symlink and a gitlink in place of the directory, and at pinned offset 16000). The selected file's page also shows another file's diff. Make the patch cover only the exact selected entry, or run the whole-file check on every path the pathspec expands to (`git diff --name-only -z` with the same pathspec) and fail closed when any of them, or the expansion itself, can't be checked. Add tests for a directory replaced by a file, a symlink and a gitlink.

original.title: git add -A in commitAll still runs a nested repository's filter
original.detail: The new flag covers only commands named status or diff. `git add -A` runs its own status inside a populated nested repository (GIT_TRACE shows `cd nested; GIT_DIR=.git git status --porcelain=2 -uno`). Reproduced with real git 2.54 at this head: a committed gitlink plus a committed `.gitmodules` entry with `ignore = none`, then a clean filter configured in the nested repository's own .git/config, `* filter=...` in its info/attributes, its file's mtime changed and an ordinary parent file edited. `commitAll()` ran the filter (marker created) and returned a commit. The new test misses this because its second call advances the nested HEAD. Make every staging call on an agent-writable checkout (commitAll, merge completion, the eval runners' add calls) skip nested work-tree inspection even when committed `.gitmodules` asks for it, while added and changed gitlink commits are still staged and audited. Add a regression test with an unchanged existing gitlink and `ignore = none`.

original.title: An attributes file left by setup changes the bytes the reset restores
original.detail: `git reset --hard -q <head>` reads working-tree attributes, and setup runs the case's own install scripts, so it can leave an untracked `.gitattributes` that survives the reset and rewrites tracked files on checkout. Reproduced with real git 2.54: committed `CURRENT.txt` = `new` (6e6577); setup writes `CURRENT.txt working-tree-encoding=UTF-16LE` to an untracked `.gitattributes`; after the plain reset the file holds 6e0065007700, so the reviewer reads a different case while preparation reports success (Codex reproduced it through the eval runner under the real Seatbelt profile). `git --attr-source=HEAD reset --hard -q HEAD` restores 6e6577. Take attributes from the committed tree when restoring (git's `--attr-source=<head>`, or equivalent neutral attributes), keep setup's ignored and untracked outputs, and add a test where setup writes an untracked `.gitattributes` and the reviewer still sees the committed bytes.

original.title: Merge still runs a nested repository's filter when .gitmodules no longer maps the gitlink
original.detail: `submoduleFlags` overrides `submodule.<name>.ignore` only for names in the current `.gitmodules` (worktree file, else index or HEAD). A gitlink without a current mapping keeps the committed configuration for git's internal dirty checks. Reproduced at this head with real git 2.54: a tracked populated gitlink, a committed `.gitmodules` with `ignore = none`, a clean filter in the nested repository's own config, then only the worktree `.gitmodules` emptied. `prepareMerge` ran the filter (trace: `git stash create`, then `cd nested; GIT_DIR=.git git status --porcelain=2 -uno`). Codex also reproduced it with an include-only file and a changed path mapping, and adding the HEAD name's override by hand still failed. Name-specific overrides can't cover this. Make the protection independent of `.gitmodules`: the factory never populates submodules itself, so either refuse with a clear reason before any merge, rebase or other command with an internal dirty check runs in a checkout that contains a populated nested repository (a gitlink path or untracked directory holding `.git`), or prove another mechanism with tests. Cover an emptied, include-only and remapped `.gitmodules`.

original.title: stageAll fails on file and directory replacements that add -A handles

original.title: A conflicted .gitmodules makes rebase cleanup throw before it can abort
original.detail: `submoduleFlags` throws `Cannot inspect submodule configuration` when it can't parse `.gitmodules`. After a rebase that leaves conflict markers in `.gitmodules`, the wrapper throws before `rebaseOnto`'s `rebase --abort` runs, so the rebase directory stays active (reproduced by Codex with conflicting section-name edits; plain `git rebase --abort` then succeeded). Abort and cleanup commands must always run; don't let configuration parsing block them, and keep failing closed only for commands that would otherwise run a dirty check. Add a test with a conflicted `.gitmodules`.

original.title: Targeted retry arguments are Bun path filters, so the retry can run files that never failed
original.detail: Only names starting with '-' get a './' prefix. Bun treats any other relative argument as a substring filter over test paths. Reproduction (Bun 1.4.2): files a.test.ts, data.test.ts and test/a.test.ts; `bun test 'a.test.ts'` ran all 3 files, `bun test './a.test.ts'` ran 1. Codex reproduced the same with test/a.test.ts and other/test/a.test.ts: the bare form also ran the unrelated failing file and exited 1. So a targeted retry can confirm a failure in a file that passed in the original run, and the five-file bound for skipping the gate slot does not bound what actually runs. Fix: prefix every validated relative name with './' (keep the quoting), and add a test where a failing file name is a substring of another file's path.

original.title: The targeted retry runs files without the per-file isolation the full check has
original.detail: The full check runs `bun test --parallel=...`, and `bun test --help` says --parallel implies --isolate (a fresh global object per file). The retry template `bun test {files}` runs every file in one shared global. Reproduction: two files that each read and then set globalThis.owner, expecting it unset first. `bun test --parallel=1 ./a.test.ts ./b.test.ts` passes both; `bun test ./a.test.ts ./b.test.ts` fails b (it sees a's value). A targeted retry of two or more files can therefore fail when the full check would pass. After the change that becomes a false regression with no full rerun. On the baseline it is worse: the base check stays failing, and a check that fails on base never blocks, so a real regression in that check is not blocking for the whole run. Codex reproduced that end to end: retryBaselineFailures kept the baseline failing, and compareGates then returned still_failing with blocking=false for a candidate failure. Fix: `retry_files = "bun test --isolate {files}"`, with a test that two files leaking a global pass in a targeted retry.

original.title: The baseline cache stores the new failure-file fields before redaction

original.title: A targeted retry that skips the gate slot keeps the check's full timeout
original.detail: The bypass checks the earlier JUnit duration (at most 60 s over at most 5 files), but the retry inherits the check's timeoutSec (1800 s here). A file that hangs on retry (an intermittent deadlock is a common flake) then runs outside the gate slot for up to 30 minutes, holding one of the two agentTestSlots that implementers' test runs share. The duration also comes from a report written by the run under test, so it is a hint, not a limit. Reproduction (Codex): parse a report with `<testsuite file="test/a.test.ts" failures="1" time="0"/>`, then call retryRegressions; the runner receives targeted=true, skipGateSlot=true and the unchanged 1800 s timeout. Fix: when a retry skips the slot, cap its timeout at a small multiple of the bound (for example 2 x UNSLOTTED_RETRY_MAX_SECONDS). A targeted timeout already falls through to the slotted full retry, so the cap enforces the bound without losing the check. Apply it once, in retryFailures, so the baseline and regression paths share it. Add a test that the unslotted request carries the capped timeout and that a timeout leads to the full retry.

original.title: A confirmed targeted failure replaces the full check's output, so the implementer can miss failures the report doesn't list
original.detail: When the targeted retry fails, the result becomes `{ ...attempt, firstAttempt, targetedRetry }`, and formatGateFeedback shows only that attempt's command and output. Bun's JUnit report leaves out a test file that throws while loading. Reproduction (Bun 1.4.2): c.test.ts throws at top level and d.test.ts has a failing test; the command exits 1, but the report lists only d.test.ts and parseJUnit returns failedFiles ["d.test.ts"]. The targeted retry of d fails again, the regression is confirmed (correctly), but the feedback no longer shows c.test.ts's load error, which costs the implementer an extra round. Classification is unaffected, because a targeted pass always goes on to the full retry. Fix: when a targeted retry confirms the failure, keep the original full run as the visible result (command and output) and attach the targeted attempt as targetedRetry; or include the first attempt's output in the feedback. Add a test that the feedback for a confirmed targeted failure still contains the original output.

original.title: Pairing can't detect a relay between worker and coordinator
original.detail: The worker accepts any certificate on its first request, prints the code the server returned, and pins whatever fingerprint it observed. The displayed code is chosen by the server and is not bound to either TLS endpoint, so comparing the two codes cannot show that the worker reached a different machine. Reproduction (Codex): two loopback TLS listeners, one relaying /worker/pair and /worker/pair/claim to the coordinator. Both displayed codes matched, pairWorker saved the relay's fingerprint instead of the coordinator's, and the token the relay received then authenticated to the coordinator. Fix: derive the displayed code independently on each side from values each side observed: the coordinator from its own certificate fingerprint, the worker fingerprint in the request and a server nonce; the worker from the coordinator fingerprint it observed on the TLS socket, its own fingerprint and the nonce from the reply. The worker must print its locally derived code, never a code from the response. In the same probe, independently derived codes differed through the relay. Add a test with an in-process relay showing the codes differ, and one showing they match on a direct connection.

original.title: The coordinator key and worker credentials are read-denied only while a listener or worker process holds them
original.detail: protectPrivateFile runs inside certificate() and privateFile(), so a path is protected only while that call's holder is alive. startWorkerListener returns before certificate() when [workers] listen is unset, and the worker files are protected only inside the `limitless worker` process. Its registrations don't reach agents launched by a daemon on the same machine, and runWorker never protects worker/key.pem. The API token (src/server/api-token.ts) and the database (src/db/store.ts) are protected for the daemon's whole lifetime. Reproduction (Codex, real Seatbelt): start and stop the listener, then start with listen unset; an editor profile built through homeReadPolicy could read the retained worker-tls/key.pem, while the active listener's profile denied it. With a worker running against the same data home, sandboxed reads of worker/token, worker/key.pem and worker/coordinator-fingerprint succeeded. Fix: at daemon start, before integrations or runs start and whether or not a listener is configured, protect worker-tls/key.pem, worker/token, worker/key.pem and worker/coordinator-fingerprint, and keep them protected until shutdown. Also protect worker/key.pem in runWorker. Extend the real-Seatbelt test to start the daemon's protection with listen unset and probe all four paths.

original.title: The pairing claim secret is not registered for redaction

original.title: Expired pairing requests accumulate past the pending cap and still list as pending
original.detail: The 100-request cap counts only unexpired rows, and nothing removes expired ones. Reproduction (Codex, injected clock): create 100 requests, advance 600001 ms, and repeat three times. The table holds 300 pending rows and list() shows all 300 as pending. The unauthenticated pairing route can therefore grow the table and the owner's `workers ls` without bound. Fix: delete expired pending rows when a pairing is created (the same transaction as the count), and show only unexpired requests as pending. Add a test with the injected clock.

original.title: A 40-bit pairing code built from a relay-chosen nonce can be matched offline
original.detail: pairWorker derives its code from the nonce in the first reply, which a relay controls, and the code keeps only 40 bits (8 base32 characters). A relay learns the coordinator's code for its relayed request: it's in the reply, and it can also be computed from the public coordinator fingerprint, the forwarded worker fingerprint and the server nonce. The relay can then search substitute nonces offline until the worker's locally derived code matches, without any more coordinator requests. Reproduction (Codex): pairingCode runs at 1.73 million calls/s on one core in JS. With coordinator 'a'x64, relay 'b'x64, worker 'c'x64 and server nonce 'd'x64, the coordinator code was 6Z3ZW638. A search over substitute nonces found one giving 6Z3ZL7RH (first four characters equal) after 905,736 tries in 0.56 s. A full match is about 2^40 work: 7 days in JS on one core, about 18 minutes at 1e9 hashes/s, and less on a current GPU. That is within reach of the pairing window. Fix: compare a value of at least 80 bits. For example, derive 16 base32 characters with the same inputs, show them on both sides in groups of four, and accept the full value in `limitless workers approve`. Alternatively, use a commit/reveal exchange so neither side's contribution can be chosen after seeing the other's. Note that a public worker nonce alone doesn't prevent the adaptive choice. Add a test that the comparison value carries at least 80 bits, and keep the relay tests.

original.title: A claim after a coordinator restart doesn't re-register the claim secret for redaction
original.detail: The secret is registered only when pair() generates it, so a claim served by a restarted coordinator (a fresh process with the same database) leaves the incoming secret unregistered. Reproduction (Codex): create and approve a pairing in a file-backed database, start a fresh Bun process, reopen it and call claim(secret). The claim succeeds, but redactCredentials(secret) still returns the plaintext. The existing restart test recreates WorkerStore inside one process, so the global registry from the first process masks the gap. Fix: register a well-formed incoming claim secret in claim() before using it, and test it in a fresh process (or with the credential registry reset).

original.title: Replace the quotation-context gate with a per-author provenance rule; add no new patterns
original.detail: Round 1 ran five fix-and-review loops. Each one tuned a quotation-context gate for short private matches ('Quoted: …'), and each review found a wrapper that defeats it: a bare link `[red owl](u)`, then an image `![red owl](u)`. Nothing was pushed, so the PR is still at 58efddc. Build round 2 from 58efddc. #516 is amended (see the issue's 2026-10-16 section). Keep the structural part: private verifier rows rendered as marked spans and dropped whole. Remove the quotation-context requirement entirely, and decide the prose backstop by who wrote the line. Text the verifier wrote (notes, and evidence on public criteria) is matched against every private verifier string and holdout scenario text. The implementer's report is matched against the private-row summaries the implementer actually received in verify feedback (`formatVerifyFeedback` gives it `publicSummary` after `redactHoldoutText`), and never against private-row evidence or citations it didn't see. Other prose gets harvested literals only. Before matching, normalize: decode HTML entities; unescape Markdown escapes; strip link and image syntax, emphasis, inline code, blockquote markers and table pipes while keeping label text; collapse whitespace across line breaks and join mid-word wraps; then scan every offset so overlapping matches are found. Match before any clipping, or clip only at line or span boundaries. Tests, each of which must fail at 58efddc: (a) the verifier's notes and its public-criterion evidence quote a private phrase plain, as a link, as an image, emphasised, as inline code, in a blockquote, in a table cell, entity-encoded, wrapped across lines, and wrapped mid-word, and every form is withheld; (b) the same forms in the implementer's report, for a private-row summary it received, are withheld; (c) two overlapping private phrases are both withheld; (d) gap 4's generic wording ('All checks passed.' as private-row evidence the implementer never received) stays visible in the implementer's report; (e) the same wording is withheld in the verifier's notes. Keep the existing #514 tests passing.

original.title: An identity-inspection failure after SIGSTOP leaves the frozen process stopped forever
original.detail: On any error, the catch block re-runs processBirth for each claimed member before its SIGKILL, inside `try { … } catch {}`. If that inspection throws as well (proc_pidinfo failing with an errno other than ESRCH, for example), the SIGKILL is silently skipped and the member stays in state T. That breaks the code's own rule, 'Never leave a frozen member behind'. Reproduction (Codex, temporary test with an owned /bin/sleep and real signal delivery): make darwinProcessBirth throw for that PID after its SIGSTOP. runProcess rejects, the recorded signals are only ['SIGSTOP'], and ps shows the sleeper in state T. Fix: never leave a member that this sweep froze in the stopped state. A process this sweep stopped can't exit by itself, so while it stays stopped its PID can't be reused. If its identity can't be re-confirmed after bounded retries, still SIGKILL the members this sweep froze, and report the inspection failure in the thrown error. Keep refusing to signal any PID this sweep never froze. Add a test with injected inspection failures (thrown after the freeze, and again in the error path) that ends with no stopped member and an error naming the failure.

original.title: 'kept growing' is reported for ordinary discovery of an existing tree
original.detail: `growing` becomes true as soon as any PID is claimed after the first populated scan, so a tree that existed before cleanup started, but was discovered over two scans, is reported as 'set kept growing'. Reproduction (Codex): start two sleepers before cleanup, expose one in the first injected snapshot and both afterwards, suppress their signals and advance the clock to the deadline. The error reports 2 processes and 'set kept growing', although neither forked. #537 asks for this to tell a forking tree apart from a slow machine. Fix: count growth from process birth times, using members born after the cleanup started (processBirth already returns the start time), instead of from discovery order. Add that case as a test.

original.title: An expired reservation still runs the work unslotted while the daemon is answering
original.detail: When a reply says the queued reservation expired (`{acquired:false, expired:true}`, which happens after a daemon restart, for example), the ordinary path throws 'gate-slot lease expired'. The outer catch then warns and runs `work()` unslotted, which is the case #554 forbids, because the daemon is clearly reachable. Reproduction (Codex, fake client and clock): reply `{id:'q', acquired:false}`, advance 250 ms, then reply `{id:'q', acquired:false, expired:true}`. With maxWaitMs 60000 the work runs unslotted with the warning. With maxWaitMs 0 the expiry check is skipped and the caller polls 'q' forever, even after capacity is free, which is a regression from main. Fix: for ordinary callers, treat an expired reservation as 'request a new reservation' (clear the id and keep waiting under the same responsive rule). Agent-test lanes keep their LeaseRejected. Add tests for both maxWait values.

original.title: Progress lines always say 'unknown holder' because ordinary lease replies carry no holder
original.detail: The ordinary `/api/admin/gate-slot` reply never includes `holder`, so `limitless deploy` and `limitless gate-slot` print 'holder: unknown holder' every 3 minutes, although the semaphore knows who holds the slot. #554 asks for the holder in the progress lines. Reproduction (Codex): occupy the semaphore as 'pipeline visible-holder', use a fake client with the endpoint's real reply shape, and advance the clock. Both the 180 s and 360 s lines say 'unknown holder'. The new test hides this by injecting `holder` into the fake reply. Fix: include the current holder (redacted) in ordinary busy replies on the daemon side, and test through the real reply shape.
