original.title: The growth diagnostic's clock can fail cleanup and is read on every child exit
original.detail: bornAt = birthClock() runs before discovery on every child exit, including invocations with nothing left to claim. On Linux that reads /proc/self/auxv and /proc/uptime each time, and if either is unreadable or AT_CLKTCK is missing it throws. stopMarkedProcesses then fails before any scan: runProcess rejects with ProcessTerminationError and the scope latches the error, so later commands are refused. Reproduction (Codex): a Linux-backend fixture with valid ancestry and empty discovery but auxv or uptime unavailable; `exit 0` rejected, and with readable fixtures it succeeded. A diagnostic must not decide whether cleanup succeeds ('Fail closed, precisely'). Fix: read the clock only when a member is first claimed. If it can't be read, report growth as unknown and keep cleaning up. Add a test with the clock failing and nothing to claim, and one with a member to claim.

original.title: Growth comparison ignores the clocks' precision
original.detail: On macOS the cleanup clock is Date.now() * 1000 (millisecond precision), while process birth is in microseconds, so a member born earlier in the same millisecond compares as newer. Reproduction (Codex): an owned sleep spawned before sampling had birth 1792169203:23704 against a cleanup clock of 1792169203023000. On Linux, /proc/uptime (10.03) times 100 Hz gives 1002.9999999999999, so starttime 1003 from the same tick counts as growth. Fix: compare conservatively at the coarser precision (macOS: birth > clock + 1000 µs; Linux: birth > floor(uptime * hz) + 1 tick, computed in integers). Add both boundary cases to the growth test.each.

original.title: Keep complete span sources out of report.md, and give every clipped field one clipping path
original.detail: Each clipped span's complete `source` is stored in the base64 manifest inside report.md. The previous release's getChange (b2cc31f, the main this PR merged) knows no manifests, so after a rollback it returns the footer line unfiltered on both MCP backends. Decoding it recovers private verifier text that the displayed report never contained. Reproduction (Codex): verifier notes hold an unclipped private tail, and 310 characters of public-row evidence are followed by that tail. renderReport stores the full evidence in the footer, and b2cc31f's getChange returns it decodable. Clipping is also still only half covered (round-2 finding 3). Criterion cells and other escapeCell output clip without a source. Reproduction (Codex, both backends): a criterion of 280 characters followed by ' the **amber** lantern glows ultraviolet' (private evidence quotes that phrase) shows 'the **amber** lante'. Fix: (1) report.md and its footer carry only the displayed text, span offsets and the digest. Store complete sources in a separate artifact (for example report-sources.json, keyed to the report digest) that only this release's change view reads. With no sources artifact or a digest mismatch, withhold any clipped span whole. GET /api/runs/:id/artifacts/<name> is owner-authenticated (API token or session; agents can't read the token), as holdout-scenarios.json already is, so that route is not a new exposure. (2) Every clipped field (implementer summary, criterion, evidence and any other escapeCell output outside a private span) goes through one clipping helper that records its source. Tests: the footer decodes to offsets and a digest only; a clipped span with a missing sources artifact is withheld; and the criterion-clip reproduction above is withheld.

original.title: Spec-written criteria in public rows get the verifier's strict matcher
original.detail: A public acceptance row is marked as verifier text as a whole, so the criterion cell, which the spec wrote, is matched against every private string. Reproduction (Codex, both backends): a met private row with evidence 'All checks passed.' and the public AC-1 criterion 'All checks passed.' with evidence 'Ran public command successfully.' The whole public row disappears. Fix: apply the strict set to the evidence cell only (for example a source that holds only the evidence), and match the criterion cell against the harvested literals, as for other spec text. If evidence matches, the row is withheld as now. Add this case as a test.

original.title: Resolve the conflict with #548: keep run state literal, keep the baseline cache redacted, move #548's test assertions accordingly
original.detail: The PR conflicts with main. The automatic conflict round (mvb4r4dm06licf41wa3ubi, unpushed at 6b8522d) ended needs_human, because #548's test 'baseline targeted evidence is redacted before caching' (test/gate-executor.test.ts, both pass values) fails. On main, #548 redacts the baseline before it enters run state (`return redactGateData(retried)` in runBaseline's retry, and the cache read returns redactGateData(cached)), and its test asserts that state.baseline holds '[redacted].test.ts'. That contradicts #494: failedFiles and targetedRetry.command are executable inputs, so run state stays literal, and a resumed targeted retry must run the real file. 6b8522d kept state literal, but its cache write `store.putBaselineCache(key, fresh, ...)` now stores the literal run, so the shared cross-run cache would hold the credential. That regresses #548's fix. Resolution: merge main; keep state.baseline literal; write the cache as `putBaselineCache(key, redactGateData(fresh), ...)`; keep the cached read redacted as on main; keep baseline-gates.json and events going through the outward redaction. Update #548's test to match, without weakening it: assert state.baseline keeps the literal failedFiles and targeted command, while the passing_baselines row, the baseline-gates.json artifact and the events don't contain the secret (row and artifact equal redactGateData(state.baseline)). Run ./test/gate-executor.test.ts, ./test/pipeline-baseline-cache.test.ts and ./test/pipeline-gates.test.ts.

original.title: JSON-encoded prompt inputs hide escape-split credentials from invoke-time redaction
original.detail: Invoke-time redaction (context.ts:773, redactGateOutput on the final prompt) runs after values were JSON-encoded, and JSON.stringify turns an ESC byte into the six characters \u001b, which stripVTControlCharacters does not remove. So a registered credential split by an escape sequence survives. Reproduction: registerCredential('probe', 'synthetic-panel-credential-549'); a stored finding title 'leak synthetic-panel\x1b[31m-credential-549 here'; redactGateOutput(JSON.stringify({ title }, null, 2)) keeps 'synthetic-panel\u001b[31m-credential-549', and parsing the JSON and dropping the SGR sequence recovers the full credential. On main the title was sanitized on load ('leak [redacted] here'). Reviewer verification via verifierPrompt (candidates, line 601) shows the same through RunContext with the fake harness. AGENTS.md: decode before you redact. Fix: sanitize values before encoding them (one helper, e.g. JSON.stringify(redactGateData(value), ...)) at every site that JSON-encodes run state into model or outward text: prompts.ts 490, 503, 593, 594 and 601, engine.ts 818 (offending spec sentence fed back to the spec model) and engine.ts 2072, plus any other prompt builder that JSON-encodes state. Add a test with an escape-split credential in a stored finding that fails without the fix.

original.title: Shadow review resume compares a literal range with the redacted artifact
original.detail: review-N.shadow.json now goes through ctx.artifact, which redacts it, but shadowReview still uses that artifact as its resume checkpoint and compares prior.range with the literal range. Any range text that redaction changes (a registered credential that matches part of a SHA or range; Codex reproduced it with a 40-hex synthetic credential used as baseSha) makes a completed shadow review look incomplete. It then re-runs and replaces the completed artifact with 'skipped'. The previous head kept 'completed'. Fix: compare against the same canonical form as the stored copy (redactGateOutput(range)), or keep the literal checkpoint in run state instead of the outward artifact.

original.title: Leased requests send credential-bearing gate commands to the worker
original.detail: The lease reply sends the full GateRequest; it removes only cwd. original.detail: scratch falls back to TMPDIR or os.tmpdir(), and the inherited TMPDIR is added even when invocationScratch exists. original.title: A land retry must require complete failure attribution; otherwise it can land a suite that also failed elsewhere
original.detail: Factory gates follow a targeted pass with a full-suite retry. Land checks skip that, so the targeted retry is safe only when every failure in the first run is attributed to a listed file. Today it isn't required. Reproductions (Codex, fake land executor): (1) JUnit `<testsuites errors="1"><testsuite file="README.md" failures="1" errors="0"/></testsuites>` with exitCode 1. parseJUnit ignores root counters and accepts unmatched suite-level counts, so retrying README.md alone lands the entry. A parent-level error and a well-formed report missing a failing case do the same. (2) exitCode 1, a JUnit report attributing one failure to README.md, and output containing `# Unhandled error between tests … 1 error`. The targeted pass lands; a load-error variant also lands. Fix: allow the land retry only when attribution is complete. Every failure and error counter at every JUnit level must be matched by failing test cases in the listed files, and the runner's own summary must agree, with no unhandled errors, load errors or extra error count. When completeness can't be established, block as today. Keep the factory gates' behaviour unchanged. Test each reproduction.

original.title: A failure whose stack is in another test file of the run is attributed to the file that happened to be running
original.detail:
Reproduced on Bun 1.4.2 without --parallel. test/a.test.ts has a passing test that keeps a setTimeout loop alive and rejects a Promise once globalThis.active is set; test/b.test.ts sets globalThis.active = true and sleeps 100 ms. `bun test --reporter=junit --reporter-outfile=report.xml ./test/a.test.ts ./test/b.test.ts` reports `1 pass`, `1 fail`, `Ran 2 tests across 2 files.`; JUnit marks test/b.test.ts failed with `<failure type="Error" message="leaked from a">Error: leaked from a

original.title: Worker results with the new failureAttributionComplete field are rejected, so LAN gates fail and the test check reports a confinement error
original.detail: The round merges current main, which has #570's worker protocol. `Check` in src/workers/protocol.ts is a strict zod object, and GateResult now carries `failureAttributionComplete`, so every worker result fails validation ("Invalid gate result or requested checks"). Reproduced: this PR merged with main fails test/workers.test.ts 'invalid sha result fails infrastructure and preserves the failing local outcome' (receives 'Invalid gate result' instead of the SHA error). In the factory's confined gate the same rejection makes 'a worker runs real checks from the exact bundle head…' and the LAN retry tests fall back to local execution outside the test's fake confinement; that fallback applies a real Seatbelt profile inside the gate's own, its error output makes the whole `test` check a CONFINEMENT ERROR, and all five round-2 attempts were blocked by it. The confinement error is a symptom: don't change sandbox code or test confinement for it. Fix: add `failureAttributionComplete: z.boolean().optional()` to `Check`, add a workers test that a result carrying the field is accepted and reaches the land retry decision, and run ./test/workers.test.ts with the other affected files. Compatibility: an older coordinator's strict schema rejects results from a newer worker that send the field, so document in docs/GUIDE.md next to the worker setup that the coordinator must be upgraded before its workers (the GUIDE already says to keep them on the same release).

original.title: Production verifiers are not confined readers: the fix and the smoke probe must cover the unconfined slotted-command path
original.detail: The verify stage (src/pipeline/engine.ts around line 1721) calls ctx.invoke without confineReads; only holdout (engine.ts around 985) sets confineReads: true. So the new claude.ts read allowance for Bun's executable never applies to the verifiers reported in #576, #584 and #581. Those run unconfined with the lease wrappers from withSlottedCommands (src/pipeline/context.ts around line 846): `bun test` goes through the agent-test lease wrapper, whose loopback lease connection the Claude reader sandbox refuses (EPERM), and the wrapper waits instead of failing. The EPERM pre-connection handling in src/cli/agent-test.ts is the fix that matters for them. Required: add (or restore) an unconfined verifier-mode check that builds the spec the way ctx.invoke builds verifier specs, including withSlottedCommands([["bun","test"]], …), and shows a one-assertion `bun test` completes within a short bound; keep the confined probe if useful, but rename it and its tests so they don't claim to be the verifier configuration. Also make sure the EPERM path ends promptly with a clear outcome (bounded, no silent pass): say in the report what the wrapper does on EPERM and test it.

original.title: The worker setup warning is written before the local rerun and never clears
original.detail: fallbackSetup() writes workers.setup_warning as soon as a worker reports a failed setup, before the local rerun has run. When the local setup also fails (the change itself broke setup, which the 'local setup failure blocks' test exercises), the worker is still flagged, so `limitless workers ls` blames a healthy worker. Issue #595 asks to show a setup MISMATCH: the worker's setup failed while the same request's setup passed locally. Nothing ever clears the warning either: not a later successful worker job, not a worker restart or reconnect, only revoking and re-pairing (INSERT OR REPLACE). So a worker whose environment was fixed stays flagged. Write the warning only after the local rerun's setup passes. Clear it when that worker next completes a job whose setup succeeds (or when it re-registers on a new release), and guard the clear so it doesn't erase a newer warning written meanwhile. Add tests: a local setup failure leaves the worker unflagged; a passing local rerun flags it; a later successful worker setup clears it.

original.title: Setup reruns for every retry that has a runner, including local retries in the same checkout
original.detail: retryFailures now keeps cfg.setup whenever a runner is passed (lines 283 and 306), but a runner doesn't mean a fresh checkout: the engine's baseline and regression retries and the land queue's local retries all pass one and run in the first attempt's checkout. Rerunning setup there can invalidate output an earlier, passing check produced. For example, setup cleans dist, a build check recreates it, and a test fails transiently. The retry cleans dist again and reruns only the test, so a transient failure becomes a persistent one. The engine comment 'Retry before resetting, so a check sees the same build output as its first attempt' relies on that not happening. Keep setup only when the retry may run in a different checkout, i.e. when it goes through an executor that gives each job its own checkout (the LAN executor for a repository in [workers] repos), the case the removed runGateExecution workaround handled. Local retries keep setup: []. Use one rule for the land queue and the engine paths, and add a local-retry test with a setup that removes an earlier check's output, asserting the retry doesn't rerun it.

original.title: A worker that lost its claim can still merge
original.detail: After the owned() transaction, mergePullRequest (src/git/repos.ts ~1447) awaits a PR lookup and can retry before it runs `gh pr merge`. If another worker reclaims the entry during that lookup and blocks or re-checks it, the stale worker still merges the unchanged SHA: --match-head-commit checks the SHA, not the land claim, and the heartbeat notices the loss only on its next tick (nominally 10 s, unbounded under an event-loop stall). Re-check ownership synchronously immediately before invoking the merge command (after every await inside mergePullRequest), and abort the worker's signal as soon as a heartbeat or check sees the claim lost. Add a test that reclaims during the pre-merge lookup and asserts no merge command runs.

Gate every classifier write the land queue triggers on the same ownership check (a guard callback the classifier must call inside each write transaction), or have the classifier return its intended writes for the queue to apply under owned(). original.title: After a rollback, the previous release can deliver a resolution-only head as completed findings work
original.detail: The new reviewResolution field is storage-compatible, but its checkpoint isn't safe across a rollback. If a deploy rolls back to the previous release after the resolution round's checks complete but before reviewResolution.sha is recorded (for example a quick-profile round), the persisted conflictRound, implementation and cached approving review look to the old buildLoop like a finished conflict round. It proceeds straight to delivery and pushes the resolution merge without ever implementing the findings, reporting the round as done. AGENTS.md 'Compatibility with the running release' requires the previous release to keep working. Persist the in-progress resolution in a form the previous release refuses or treats as needing a human (for example don't reuse conflictRound for the resolution step, or record a state the old engine rejects), and add a test that loads the mid-resolution state with the previous engine's logic, or asserts the persisted state can't be read as a completed conflict round.

original.title: A completed pending merge with MERGE_HEAD still present now passes the delivery guard
original.detail: For the current head with pendingRebaseSha set, assertDeliveryHead now calls validateMerge with the commit SHA instead of "HEAD", which skips the "Completed merge still has MERGE_HEAD" check in src/git/merge.ts. The old code ran that check for pending merges. Concrete state: a crash leaves the pending merge M=[R,F1] committed (HEAD=M, HEAD !== preRebaseHead) with MERGE_HEAD still present. The guard now accepts it; mergeForDelivery → prepareMerge then fails on the same condition with a generic Error, and because that error is not a DeliveryHeadError the failure path publishes a verified-work draft (deliverVerifiedDraft) where the guard previously suppressed publication entirely. Skip the MERGE_HEAD check only where it is legitimately expected: a historical link in the chain, or a current HEAD that equals preRebaseHead while the pending merge (MERGE_HEAD = pendingRebaseSha) is still uncommitted. A current HEAD that is itself the completed pending merge must be validated as "HEAD" with the MERGE_HEAD check, and that failure must stay a DeliveryHeadError. Add a test for this state that asserts the run ends with the delivery refusal and publishes nothing (no push, no draft PR); keep the existing "merge still in progress" resume test passing.

original.title: The digest drops blocked lands of PRs that no run owns

original.title: A cleanup error can now leave the live direct child running
original.detail: On a cleanup error, terminate used to SIGKILL the directly spawned child unconditionally ("ours even if process discovery is unavailable"). With a cleanup scope it now first reads the child's birth and records it, and skips child.kill() when that read throws or returns null, or when an earlier ownership write failed. On darwin processBirth throws "Native process inspection is unavailable" without the native module, which is exactly the discovery failure the old comment covered, so the child keeps running (and can keep writing to the checkout); a failed first write also leaves no recovery row. The live direct child (exitCode and signalCode both null) can't have a reused PID, so it must always be killed: record it first when its identity can be read, but never let a failed read or write prevent the kill, and keep that failure in the termination error. Better still, capture and persist the direct child's identity right after spawn so it is recorded before any cleanup starts. Change the new test that currently asserts the child survives so it asserts the child is killed.

original.title: On Linux a record from before a reboot can match and SIGKILL an unrelated process
original.detail: Linux processBirth returns only the boot-relative start time in clock ticks (/proc/<pid>/stat field 22). process_cleanups rows survive a reboot (and a rollback followed by a later upgrade), and after a reboot PIDs and start ticks repeat, so an unrelated process with the same PID and start tick passes the identity check and gets SIGKILL. That breaks "never signal a process you did not start". Persist the boot identity with each record (Linux /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id; on macOS the birth is absolute, but recording kern.boottime keeps one rule) and retire records from another boot without signalling. The table is new in this PR, so change it in place. Add a test where a record from another boot matches a live process's PID and birth and is never signalled.

original.title: Recovery waits on zombies and kills one member at a time
original.detail: Recovery SIGKILLs one recorded member, then polls processBirth until it changes, for up to 10 s, before touching the next member. On Linux processBirth still returns the start time for a zombie (/proc/<pid>/stat exists), so a killed member whose parent is another recorded member that is still SIGSTOPped (frozen by the interrupted sweep, not yet killed) stays a zombie: recovery times out with "Recorded process still alive", stops, and leaves the frozen parent and its rows behind. Live cleanup already treats zombie state as gone (stillRunning). SIGKILL every confirmed member of the invocation first, then wait for all of them under one deadline, using the same zombie-aware liveness check as live cleanup. Add a Linux-path test with a stopped recorded parent and a recorded child where the child's row comes first.

original.title: Matching records by command directory blocks unrelated runs
original.detail: recoverProcessCleanups selects other runs' records whenever r.cwd equals the new command's directory. original.title: Startup recovery runs before the daemon reports healthy
original.detail: startDaemon recovers every pending record sequentially before HTTP starts, at up to 10 s per stubborn member, and the deploy's health wait allows about 45 s, so a handful of unresolved cleanups from failed or cancelled runs can make a deploy roll back even though each run is already guarded (executeRun and runProcess recover before that run's next command). original.title: The macOS boot identity changes when the clock is set, so recovery can retire our own live records
original.detail: darwinBootIdentity returns KERN_BOOTTIME, which XNU adjusts forwards or backwards whenever the calendar clock is set (osfmk/kern/clock.c, the settimeofday / time-daemon step path). If the clock is stepped between recording a member and recovering it, recovery sees a different "boot", skips signalling and deletes the record, leaving our own descendants running, which is the state this PR exists to remove. Use kern.bootsessionuuid, a read-only per-boot UUID that clock changes don't touch. Also replace the global beforeEach stub of darwinBootIdentity in test/setup.ts: it hides the real reader from every test. Stub boot identity only in the tests that need a fixed value (processBootInspection already exists for that), and add a test that calls the real darwin reader and checks it returns the same non-empty value twice; that read is denied inside the factory's confinement, so give it `test.skipIf(seatbeltSkip !== null)` with seatbeltSkip from test/confinement.ts, as AGENTS.md describes for real-Seatbelt tests.

original.title: Reporting zombies as having no birth weakens the darwin leader identity check
original.detail: This round made darwinProcessBirth (and Linux processBirth) return null for a zombie. processBirth is an identity reader, not only a liveness check: the leader validation at src/util/processes-darwin.ts ~322 accepts numeric session/group membership when `birth === leader.birth || birth === null`, treating null as "our leader exited". If the original leader's PID has been reused by an unrelated session/group leader that is a zombie at that moment, its surviving members are now accepted, claimed and signalled; before this round the zombie's differing birth rejected them. Keep processBirth returning the birth for zombies (PROC_PIDTBSDINFO reports zombies, as does /proc/<pid>/stat), and add a separate zombie-aware liveness check used only where the code waits for a killed member to go away (recovery's wait loop). Add a test that a zombie with a different birth at the leader's PID does not make its group's members claimable.

original.title: Recovery fails outright when the run's worktree no longer exists
original.detail: recoverProcessCleanups calls realpathSync(worktreePath) before looking at any records. If the run's recorded worktree has been removed (for example external removal or storage loss before a resume), it throws ENOENT: executeRun marks the run failed with a raw ENOENT, and runProcess sets a permanent terminationError, even when there are no records to recover, and it also prevents recovering the run's own records. Only canonicalize when there are records whose directory needs comparing, and don't throw for a missing worktree: match the run's own records by runId as before, and treat a missing worktree as matching no other run's records. original.title: A transient GitHub failure in the new preflight blocks the land
original.detail: The preflight `gh pr view` goes through runGh, which has no retry, and any failure becomes LandBlocked("cannot inspect current GitHub PR metadata: …"). A single 502 or timeout therefore ends a land that previously would have proceeded (there was no call at this point before), and it stays blocked until someone requeues it. The merge itself uses withGitHubRetry (src/git/repos.ts). Run the preflight lookup through the same bounded, abortable retry (one retry layer, transient errors only, the claim re-checked after the await as now); keep refusing at once on a permanent error or a response that fails validation, and on exhausted retries block with a reason that says GitHub was unavailable. Add a test where the first preflight lookup fails transiently and the land proceeds, and one where a permanent error still blocks before any check runs.

original.title: The MERGE_HEAD check reads only the first entry and treats a failed read as no merge
original.detail: The guard uses `git rev-parse -q --verify MERGE_HEAD` with allowFail. Two inconsistent states still pass it and then fail generically in prepareMerge/validateMerge, which takes the verified-draft fallback this issue removes: (1) MERGE_HEAD with pendingRebaseSha on the first line and another commit on a second line: rev-parse returns the first, the guard passes, and git would commit an octopus merge with both; (2) a MERGE_HEAD whose content isn't a full object id (abbreviated, garbage): rev-parse fails, stdout is empty, and the guard treats it as no merge in progress. Read MERGE_HEAD's contents through the hardened wrapper (`git rev-parse --git-path MERGE_HEAD`, then read the file): only a confirmed absence (the file doesn't exist) passes; otherwise require exactly one line equal to the full pendingRebaseSha; any other content or a failed read is a DeliveryHeadError. Add tests for a two-line MERGE_HEAD and an abbreviated one: both end with the delivery refusal and publish nothing.

original.title: A failed update rolls back the code but keeps the new dependencies
original.detail: After `bun install --frozen-lockfile` has run for the target's lockfile, a later failure (process.execve missing or throwing) restores HEAD but not node_modules, so the running worker's later module loads and the next manual restart use dependencies that don't match the checked-out lockfile; a partially failed install does the same. Check that process replacement is available before changing anything, and on rollback re-run `bun install --frozen-lockfile` at the original HEAD (report that failure too). Add a test where exec throws after install: the original HEAD is restored and the install runs again at it.

original.title: One transient failure disables updates until a manual restart
original.detail: `updateAttempted` latches after the first try and `updateTarget ??=` never changes, so a transient `git fetch` error or lock contention leaves the worker advertising zero slots forever: network recovery, a newer coordinator release, or a coordinator rollback to the worker's own release don't help. Track the latest release the coordinator reports; when it equals the worker's own, clear the update state and take jobs again; when it changes, start over. Retry transient failures with a bounded backoff (one retry layer, a deadline per target), keep the last failure as the warning, and don't retry a permanent validation failure (a SHA not on origin/main) for the same target. Add tests: a transient failure followed by a successful retry; a target change after a failure; a coordinator that returns to the worker's release.

original.title: The coordinator carries a stale update warning forward
original.detail: heartbeat() copies the previous updateWarning whenever a heartbeat omits it and the release is unchanged. After a failed update, a coordinator rollback to the worker's release and a manual worker restart, the clean worker keeps the old warning, and the new `json_extract(capabilities,'$.updateWarning') IS NULL` guard then stops both a successful setup from clearing setup_warning and a later setup fallback from recording its real warning. The worker sends its update state on every heartbeat, so store exactly what the current heartbeat reports (no carry-over), and keep the setup-fallback warning separate from the update warning. Add a test for the rollback-then-restart sequence.

original.title: A worker reporting an update failure breaks against the previous coordinator
original.detail: The previous release's Heartbeat schema is `.strict()`, so after a coordinator rollback a worker that sends the new `updateWarning` field gets HTTP 400, call() throws, and the heartbeat task stops the worker. Send updateWarning only to a coordinator that has advertised the update protocol (for example only after a heartbeat reply that included releaseSha), so a new worker keeps working with the previous coordinator. Add a test with a strict legacy heartbeat schema.

original.title: The macOS boot identity changes when the clock is set, so recovery can retire our own live records
original.detail: darwinBootIdentity returns KERN_BOOTTIME, which XNU adjusts forwards or backwards whenever the calendar clock is set (osfmk/kern/clock.c, the settimeofday / time-daemon step path). If the clock is stepped between recording a member and recovering it, recovery sees a different "boot", skips signalling and deletes the record, leaving our own descendants running, which is the state this PR exists to remove. Use kern.bootsessionuuid, a read-only per-boot UUID that clock changes don't touch. Also replace the global beforeEach stub of darwinBootIdentity in test/setup.ts: it hides the real reader from every test. Stub boot identity only in the tests that need a fixed value (processBootInspection already exists for that), and add a test that calls the real darwin reader and checks it returns the same non-empty value twice; that read is denied inside the factory's confinement, so give it `test.skipIf(seatbeltSkip !== null)` with seatbeltSkip from test/confinement.ts, as AGENTS.md describes for real-Seatbelt tests.

original.title: Reporting zombies as having no birth weakens the darwin leader identity check
original.detail: This round made darwinProcessBirth (and Linux processBirth) return null for a zombie. processBirth is an identity reader, not only a liveness check: the leader validation at src/util/processes-darwin.ts ~322 accepts numeric session/group membership when `birth === leader.birth || birth === null`, treating null as "our leader exited". If the original leader's PID has been reused by an unrelated session/group leader that is a zombie at that moment, its surviving members are now accepted, claimed and signalled; before this round the zombie's differing birth rejected them. Keep processBirth returning the birth for zombies (PROC_PIDTBSDINFO reports zombies, as does /proc/<pid>/stat), and add a separate zombie-aware liveness check used only where the code waits for a killed member to go away (recovery's wait loop). Add a test that a zombie with a different birth at the leader's PID does not make its group's members claimable.

original.title: Recovery fails outright when the run's worktree no longer exists
original.detail: recoverProcessCleanups calls realpathSync(worktreePath) before looking at any records. If the run's recorded worktree has been removed (for example external removal or storage loss before a resume), it throws ENOENT: executeRun marks the run failed with a raw ENOENT, and runProcess sets a permanent terminationError, even when there are no records to recover, and it also prevents recovering the run's own records. Only canonicalize when there are records whose directory needs comparing, and don't throw for a missing worktree: match the run's own records by runId as before, and treat a missing worktree as matching no other run's records. Add a test with a missing worktree path and an own-run record: the record is recovered and the run isn't failed by the lookup.

original.title: On Linux a missing stat file is accepted without confirming the process is gone
original.detail: expectProcessStopped returns on ENOENT/ESRCH from reading /proc/<pid>/stat. If procfs isn't mounted, or hides other users' processes (hidepid), a live process also gives ENOENT, so the helper passes for a running process, against the issue's requirement to stay strict about one. Before accepting a missing stat file, require `process.kill(pid, 0)` to fail with ESRCH (a zombie is already handled by the stat path); let any other outcome fail the assertion.

original.title: Encoded credentials survive the new diagnostic's redaction
original.detail: diagnose() builds the refusal message from a path with redactCredentials (which matches registered credentials literally) and redactPrivate, then calls checkPublicationText(section, name(path), []) with no entries, which enforces only the decoding limit. A file whose name contains a percent-encoded (or otherwise encoded) registered credential, in a change that also exceeds the decoding limit, therefore yields a refusal message containing the recoverable credential, and that message is stored and shown. AGENTS.md: decode before you redact. Decode the path the way the publication check does before redacting credentials and private strings, and if a decoded form still matches a credential or private entry, withhold the filename ("[redacted filename]") rather than printing it. Add a test with a percent-encoded registered credential in a filename plus oversized content: the refusal names the commit and "[redacted filename]" and never contains the encoded value.

original.title: Audit filenames are checked for private strings before they are normalized
original.detail: The finding's file is checked with privateMatches on the raw path and only then passed through redactGateOutput. A new path such as `.tmp-gate/secret-\x1b[31mhost.example.txt` doesn't match the private entry `secret-host.example` while the escape sequence is in it; redactGateOutput then strips the escape and produces the literal private string, which reaches persisted audit findings and the implementer's next-round feedback. Canonicalize first (redactGateOutput / strip terminal sequences, redact credentials), then run privateMatches on the normalized filename and replace it with "[redacted filename]" on a match. original.title: Diagnosis is quadratic in the number of files
original.detail: For every patch section, diagnose() searches the whole raw entry list (`raw.find(ids)`), so a refused change with many files does O(files²) synchronous work after the aggregate check has already refused, outside git's subprocess timeout and without observing cancellation. Index the raw entries by blob id pair (a Map) so each section is a constant-time lookup, and keep diagnosis bounded: if it can't locate the offending file within a fixed budget, rethrow the original refusal unchanged.

original.title: Recovery isn't serialized with an active live cleanup
original.detail: Recovery reads and acts on process_cleanups records without coordinating with a cleanup that is still running for the same invocation. A concurrent command in the same run (review panels and gates run invocations concurrently) can recover and SIGKILL a member that live cleanup A has frozen and is still tracking; A keeps `identity.frozen = true`, and if its later identity inspection fails, its fallback (around src/util/proc.ts:535) can SIGKILL that PID, which may by then belong to another process, without confirming its birth. Serialize live cleanup and recovery per invocation across recording, signalling and record deletion (an in-process lock keyed by invocation: recovery skips or awaits an invocation whose cleanup is active), and make concurrent recovery callers coordinate the same way. Add a regression test for this interleaving: a concurrent command's recovery must not signal members of a cleanup that is still in progress.

original.title: Recovery accepts a process group the saved leader no longer proves
original.detail: Recovery passes the persisted Darwin leader to markedProcesses, and discovery accepts numeric session/group membership when the leader's birth matches or the leader is gone (birth null, src/util/processes-darwin.ts:333). During live cleanup the group is still the invocation's. Across daemon downtime it may not be: once every original member has exited, the kernel can reuse that ID, an unrelated process can become a group leader with it and exit, and recovery then treats that group's surviving members as ours and SIGKILLs them. In recovery, use numeric group membership only while continuity is proven, for example the saved leader is still alive with its recorded birth, or a member the factory recorded and confirmed by birth is still in that group (a group ID cannot be reused while any member lives). Otherwise pass no leader, so discovery relies on markers, proven parent chains and orphan cwd. Don't change live cleanup's discovery. Add a test: saved leader gone, no confirmed recorded member alive, an unrelated process in a group with the saved ID is never signalled.

original.title: Decoding is split across separate paths, so combined encodings still escape
original.detail: HTML references are decoded only once, outside the layer loop (publicationMatches); base64 is spliced into the loop; and auditDiff adds a third pass that removes each entry's literal spelling and re-checks. Each review round has found another composition that slips through (most recently percent or HTML encoding around base64, and literal redaction destroying evidence before decoding). Replace the special cases with one decoder and one decision point: (1) in normalizedLayers, every round applies all supported decoders: percent runs, \u escapes, HTML character references (with the whitespace collapse publicationMatches does now), then base64 runs whose decoded text contains a protected value. Repeat until nothing changes, within the existing round limit (not settling stays a refusal, as now). Replacing only matching base64 runs keeps unrelated base64-looking words from affecting convergence. publicationMatches/checkPublicationText then use that matcher directly. (2) In auditDiff, decide on the terminal-escape-stripped raw file and detail, before any literal redaction, with that matcher over private entries plus registered credentials: a matching file becomes `[redacted filename]`, a matching detail `[redacted diagnostic]`, otherwise keep the text. Remove the per-entry redactLiteral pass and the separate raw-base64 pass. (3) Encodings nested inside a decoded base64 run (base64 of percent- or HTML-encoded text) stay out of scope: say so in a short comment where base64 is decoded. (4) Add one table-driven test covering, for a private entry and a registered credential, in an added file's name and in a finding's detail: percent(HTML(x)), HTML(percent(x)), percent(base64(x)), HTML-escaped base64, base64 at a non-zero byte offset (`user:` + x), and an unrelated base64-looking word that must neither redact nor refuse. original.title: A rollback after the new release boots is never recorded
original.detail: At boot the daemon clears the persisted attempt as soon as bootSha equals attempt.sha, but the deploy job is still health-checking that new daemon. If the health check then fails and `limitless deploy` rolls back (src/cli/service.ts), the rolled-back daemon finds no attempt: nothing is blocked and the feed never says the deploy failed. The reverse also happens: a boot on the old SHA while the job is still running declares failure early. The job's exit status (its status file) is the only authority for the outcome, and the caller that reads it is killed by the restart. Keep the attempt (with its job id) until its terminal status has been read; at boot and on later ticks, reconcile an unfinished attempt from that job's status file, recording success, or a block plus a deploy.failed feed item with the redacted log tail. Add tests: target boots then the job reports failure (rollback): blocked and reported; old-SHA boot while the job is still running: not judged until the status exists.

original.title: A deploy job that never writes its status stalls automatic deploys forever
original.detail: deployProcess polls the status file with no deadline and no check that the launchd job still exists, so a job that was removed, crashed before writing its status, or hung leaves AutoDeploy's `running` flag set and no later landing ever deploys; and removeDeployJob skips jobs without a status while the boot reconcile forgets the job id. Bound the wait (a deadline above `limitless deploy`'s own maximum) and detect a job that no longer exists (for example `launchctl list <label>` failing); either way record a block with a clear reason and remove the job, and keep the job id durable until its removal has succeeded. original.title: The plaintext credentials file is readable by agents
original.detail: deployProcess writes every registered credential to ~/.limitless/logs/<label>.credentials. File modes don't stop processes running as the same user, and that directory isn't in the read-deny list that tool-enabled editors and readers get (src/harness/read-policy.ts; src/harness/codex.ts), so an agent running concurrently can read all factory secrets while the file exists. original.title: Cleanup treats a failed launchctl inspection as the job being gone
original.detail: removeDeployJob (and deployJobStatus's missing-job path) treat any nonzero result of `launchctl list <label>` as absence. With allowFail a timeout returns exitCode null, so a slow launchctl makes cleanup delete the status and started marker and report success; AutoDeploy then drops the durable job id while the job may still be registered, and without the started marker a relaunch deploys again. Treat only launchctl's definite not-found result as absence; on any other failure keep the job id and markers and retry on the next tick. Add tests for a timed-out list during removal and during status checks.

original.title: A failing redaction filter can kill the deploy mid-way, or go unnoticed
original.detail: The deploy writes into the filter's pipe. If the filter throws before it starts reading stdin (missing or invalid credentials file, unlink failure), the pipe closes and the deploy's next write gets EPIPE/SIGPIPE; `limitless deploy` can then die between checking out the candidate and restarting, or during health checks, bypassing its rollback. Make the filter unable to stop reading early: on any setup error, keep draining stdin to EOF and write only a fixed `[deploy output withheld: redaction unavailable]` line (never unredacted text). Record the filter's own exit status as well and include `log unavailable` in the recorded outcome when it failed, without changing the deploy's exit status. Add a test where the filter's credentials file is invalid: the deploy command still completes and its status is recorded.

original.title: A verify-side failure now overrides a review that requested changes
original.detail: After Promise.allSettled, a rejected verify result is thrown before rejectReview runs. When review requests changes and verify fails for its own reasons (verifier models out of capacity, NoCapacityError, a structured-output failure, a NeedsHumanError raised inside the verify stage), the run now ends needs_human/failed, while before verify never ran and the round returned the review feedback to the implementer (including panel R3's own limit reason). Apply the review decision first: if review requested changes, a verify rejection other than cancellation/termination (CancelledError, SimulatedTermination, signal aborted) and `Commit changed during verification` is logged and dropped, and the round returns the review feedback; verify reruns next round. original.title: A resumed retry can rerun the verifier that just blocked

original.title: The trace report can credit trace with a defect the main reviewer already caught
original.detail: Candidates with `raisedBy: [1]` are treated as trace additions and matched against gold on their own. When the main reviewer and the trace finder report the same gold defect with titles or scenarios different enough to escape the merge, `addedOnGold` still counts it for trace, although the main report already catches that defect. The issue asks for the trace finder's findings to be reported separately (added, landed on gold, blocked a clean case), and this inflates its gold credit. Count a trace addition as landing on gold only when it matches a required defect that the main finder's own report did not catch (match the main report against gold first, then credit trace only for the remaining defects). Add a test with a main finding and a trace finding on the same gold defect under different titles: trace gets no gold credit.

original.title: A small targeted retry inside a scope that holds no slot now waits for a full gate slot
original.detail: Inside a reservation scope, `acquireGateSlot` ignores `skipGateSlot` and does `held.release ??= gateSlots.acquire(...)`. A targeted retry small enough for the unslotted lane (`retryFailures` sets `skipGateSlot` for few, short files so it uses `agentTestSlots` and never queues behind full suites) therefore takes a full gate slot whenever the scope doesn't hold one yet, and then keeps it until the scope ends. That happens under the LAN executor, the production setup, when the first attempt ran on a worker and the retry runs locally as a fallback. Reproduced with the real module: with every gate slot held by other holders, `acquireGateSlot(signal, undefined, 'retry', true)` outside a scope acquires at once; `gateSlotScope(() => acquireGateSlot(signal, undefined, 'retry', true))()` stays blocked behind the full suites. Required: a `skipGateSlot` request inside a scope that holds no gate slot keeps today's behaviour (the agent-test lane, released after that attempt, without setting the scope's reservation). When the scope already holds the gate slot, reusing it is fine. Add a test for both.

original.title: A local slot stays held while a later attempt in the same scope runs on a LAN worker
original.detail: The LAN fallback is bound into the scope, so when a worker job fails and the gate falls back to local execution, the fallback's `runLocalGates` takes the scope's reservation. The retry that follows is a new executor job, and `lanExecutor.start` enqueues it to a worker (every job for a listed repository goes to the LAN). The scope keeps the local gate slot held, unused, for the whole remote retry. With `max_concurrent_gates = 1` that blocks every other local gate on the coordinator, plus agents' slotted commands in the `gate` lane, for the length of a remote suite. The issue says retries that run on a LAN worker are unaffected. Fallbacks are not rare: 36 'LAN gates falling back to local execution' events on this installation in three days. Required: the coordinator's gate slot is never held while an attempt runs on a LAN worker. Either keep LAN-executor attempts, including their local fallbacks, on today's per-attempt acquire and release, or release the scope's reservation when an attempt in the scope is dispatched to a worker. Add a test: a scope holding a slot from a local attempt, then a LAN-dispatched attempt, lets a queued waiter take the slot.

original.title: After a rollback the previous release lands entries that are waiting for approval
original.detail: A waiting entry is stored physically as `state = 'checking'` with `approval_wait = 1`. The previous release doesn't know `approval_wait`: after a graceful shutdown (`releaseLandClaims` clears the claim) or once the claim goes stale, its `claimLandEntry` reclaims any `checking` entry and runs its own `land()`, which has no approval gate, so it checks, waits for CI and merges without anyone's approval. Reproduced: create an entry with this PR's Store, move it to `waiting_approval`, call `releaseLandClaims`, then open the same database with the deployed release's Store; `claimLandEntry('test/repo', …)` returns the entry in `checking`. A deploy rolls back automatically when the new release doesn't come up, so this gate fails open on a routine event (AGENTS.md: 'Leave the previous release working', 'Fail closed, precisely'). Required: store a waiting entry so that the previous release never lands it, for example as a state the previous release treats as finished (such as `blocked` with the approval flag; the new release reads it as `waiting_approval`, and the old one shows it blocked, needing a re-queue), or in a separate table keyed by the entry id with the entry in a non-landable state. original.title: A waiting entry holds its repository's only running land slot
original.detail: Because the waiting entry stays physically `checking` with a live claim, it occupies `land_entries_one_running` for its repository and blocks the queue's worker for as long as approval takes, possibly days. Every other PR in that repository, including ones already approved, can't start landing. Reproduced: two entries in `test/repo`; after the first moves to `waiting_approval`, `claimLandEntry('test/repo', …)` returns null for the second. Order among approved entries stays FIFO by queue time. This fits naturally with the storage change in the blocker finding. Test: entry 1 waiting, entry 2 approved, entry 2 lands first.

original.title: A stale saved snapshot can release the gate
original.detail: With polling on, `awaitApproval` reads `savedSnapshot(this.store.githubPrData(...))` with no check of when it was observed or whether the last poll succeeded. If an approval is dismissed or replaced by a change request and the next poll fails (GraphQL error, rate limit), the saved snapshot still shows the old `APPROVED` review, and a successful `user` lookup releases the entry (reproduced by Codex: save an approval, return a GraphQL error from polling, the entry moves to `checking`). Required: release only on review evidence from a successful observation made after the entry started waiting (record the observation time with the snapshot, or observe directly as the polling-off path does). A failed or stale observation leaves approval unknown, and the entry keeps waiting. Test: saved approval, then a failing poll, and the entry stays waiting.

original.title: Any GitHub account's approval counts, including accounts without push access and bots
original.detail: `hasOtherApproval` accepts any latest review in state `APPROVED` from a login other than the factory's. On a public repository anyone can submit an approving review, and on a private one a read-only member can; GitHub's own required reviews count only reviewers with write access. A bot (for example `github-actions[bot]` where the repository allows Actions to approve PRs) also counts. So the gate meant to require another person's approval can be satisfied by an account with no authority over the repository. Required: count an approval only from a `User` (not a `Bot`) with push access. GraphQL `PullRequestReview` has `authorCanPushToRepository` and `author { __typename login }`; add them to `OBSERVE_QUERY` and `reviewEvidence`, treat missing fields as no approval, and also hold the entry while any such reviewer's latest review on the PR is `CHANGES_REQUESTED`. Tests: an approval from an account without push access and one from a bot don't release the entry; an outstanding change request from a push-access reviewer keeps it waiting despite another approval.

original.title: Approval is checked once, before checks and CI, and never again before the merge
original.detail: `awaitApproval` runs before land checks; after that, checks, the CI wait and the merge (often 20 to 40 minutes, longer under load) proceed without looking at the reviews again. An approval dismissed, or a change request submitted, in that window doesn't stop the merge (AGENTS.md: 'Check-then-act across an await'). Entries that already recorded `pushedSha` skip the gate entirely, so enabling the setting while a land is in flight merges that PR without approval (reproduced by Codex: reach `waiting_ci` with the policy off, restart with it on, and the entry merges with no identity or review lookup). Required: when the policy is on, re-check immediately before `merge`, regardless of `pushedSha`, using fresh evidence as in the stale-snapshot finding. Require a qualifying approval on the approved SHA or on the pushed head, and no outstanding change request. If it fails, the entry goes back to waiting instead of merging. Tests: approval dismissed during CI doesn't merge; policy enabled with a pushed entry waits for approval.

original.title: Compound eval trials credit every model's usage to the trial's first model
original.detail: A trial without `rounds` becomes one record with `provider: details.provider` and `modelId: t.model_id`, carrying the whole trial's tokens, cost and duration. Review-eval trials with verifiers or several finders call other models too: 715 stored trials on this installation have a `details.verifiers` list (for example `claude/opus` verifiers on a `codex/sol-6.1` finder), and all of their usage is credited to the finder's provider, while the verifiers' provider shows none. Required: never attribute a compound trial's usage to a single provider or model. Where the stored data doesn't split it by member, report it in a separate compound or unattributed row that lists the participating models, and keep the per-provider rows to records that really belong to one model. Test with a stored trial that has verifiers.

original.title: Strict `[repos.*]` key validation breaks #687's key and makes every new key a rollback hazard
original.detail: `parseRepos` throws `Unknown repos key` for anything other than `discreet` and `branch_prefix`, so the daemon refuses to start. #687 (in review) adds `land_requires_approval` to the same `[repos."<owner>/<name>"]` table with its own parser. original.title: Turning discreet mode on mid-run publishes commits and reports made before the switch

The land queue likewise sends the stored `report.md` as the squash body (src/land/queue.ts `reportBody`, about line 900). A report rendered before the switch keeps the run id, local URL and branding and writes them into main's history (reproduced by Codex). Render the PR body and the squash body from the current setting at publish time instead of reusing a stored report. Tests for both.

original.title: The redactor costs time linear in the number of registered credentials and blocks the event loop for seconds
original.detail: Measured end to end with `runProcess({ cmd: ['cat', file], redactOutput: true })` streaming real invocation logs. On a 1.3 MB stream: 0 credentials 128 ms (main: 8 ms); 50 credentials 432 ms (main: 13 ms); 200 credentials 1,288 ms (main: 28 ms). On 5 MB with 600 credentials, about what a daemon holds after half a day because every agent-test session and worker claim registers a value: 19,583 ms with a single event-loop stall of 19,531 ms (main: 245 ms, worst stall 193 ms). Gate output for a full suite runs through this path in the daemon, which already stalls for up to about 20 s under load (#690), so this would freeze the API, health checks, the poller and every other run for seconds per gate. Required: the cost per byte must not grow with the number of registered credentials. For example, match all credential variants with one multi-pattern automaton (Aho-Corasick) that is rebuilt only when the registry changes, and drive it from the terminal parser's output, keeping the raw and stripped views. Bound the synchronous work per pushed chunk. Put before and after numbers for 0, 50, 200 and 600 credentials on a 5 MB stream in the PR, and keep 600 credentials within about 2× of today's time. Add a deterministic test of the complexity (for example, that matching work doesn't scale with the number of registered values), not a timing assertion. A simpler design that meets the issue's four cases is welcome. The budget was about 120 source lines, and this round's 335 grew across five rounds of fixes.

original.title: `sh` drops the timeout classification for allowFail callers, and its error text says "Command failed (0)"
original.detail: The runProcess change and the deploy-wait retries are verified (including that an exited, unreaped child counts as not running on macOS). One consumer gap remains: with `allowFail: true`, `sh` returns `{ stdout, stderr, exitCode }` only, so a child observed running at its deadline that exits 0 during cleanup looks like a clean pass. The deploy gates (`gates()` in src/cli/service.ts, which accept `exitCode === 0`) then proceed and restart the daemon after a timed-out gate. On the throwing path the message reads `Command failed (0): …`. Required: include `timedOut` (overall or idle) in `sh`'s allowFail result; make the deploy gate treat a timed-out result as a failed gate with a message that says it timed out; and when `sh` throws for a timeout, say `timed out after <n> s` instead of `Command failed (0)`. Keep `CommandError`'s existing fields. Tests: an allowFail command observed running at its deadline that exits 0 during cleanup reports `timedOut: true`, a deploy gate with that result fails, and the thrown message for a timeout names the timeout. No other changes. Run only test/proc.test.ts, test/deploy.test.ts and test/service.test.ts, `bunx biome check` on the changed files and `bunx tsc --noEmit`.

original.title: Each call still compiles a combined regex over every detail, so the stall remains (1.06x faster)
original.detail: Thank you for the differential test and the benchmark; they show exactly where the time goes. Measured in this PR: 20,000 strings took 157 s (7.9 ms each) against 166 s before, so a verify session still spends minutes of main-thread time and stalls the daemon. Measured on this PR's benchmark holdout (132 static details): a fresh combined pattern costs 5.4 ms per call including its first-use compile (JavaScriptCore compiles lazily), against 0.074 ms for a reused one; each observed literal's boundary test against the 20 KB public sources costs about 0.05 ms. The cause, as the report says, is that any value with observed literals not already in the detail set compiles a new alternation regex over all static and observed details (hundreds of Unicode lookbehind alternatives) on every call. Required: never compile a regex over the static details per call. Precompile one static pattern per invocation (sorted by length, as today). Per call, collect the value's observed private literals (with the cached publicSources boundary test), drop those already in the static set, and compile a small pattern over only the remaining observed literals, sorted by length. Then replace in one left-to-right pass that reproduces the combined alternation exactly. Using `g` regexes and `lastIndex`, find the next static match and the next observed match from the current position. Take the one that starts first; if both start at the same index, take the longer; on equal length take the static one, which comes first in today's stable sort because static details are inserted before observed ones. Replace it, continue from its end, and re-search either pattern whose pending match started before that end. Keep the `[private detail]` placeholder, the removed count and the `[n private details withheld]` suffix exactly as today. Keep the differential test (all outputs identical to the frozen implementation) and extend its generator with overlapping static/observed details, equal-length ties and adjacent matches. Rerun the benchmark: the total must fall by at least 10x and the worst call should be a few milliseconds; report both in the PR. Run only test/verification.test.ts and the other directly affected tests, `bunx biome check` on the changed files and `bunx tsc --noEmit`.

original.title: The fragment rule loops over every registered credential for each large number, making event redaction 16x slower
original.detail: The issue text was wrong here, sorry. It said numbers that are fragments of a credential follow 'the same rule that applies to strings', but strings are only redacted when they contain a registered credential, never for being part of one. The `for (const secret of credentialValues) if (secret.includes(text))` loop runs for every number of eight or more digits, and events are full of them (millisecond timestamps, token counts). Measured at production size: 20,000 events, each with seven such numbers, at 600 registered credentials, took 1,196 ms (59.8 µs per event) against 76 ms (3.8 µs) on main. It also brings back the per-credential loop that #706/#708 removed. Required: remove the fragment rule and keep only `redactCredentials(String(v)) !== String(v)` → `"[redacted]"`, which uses the shared matcher. Remove or adjust the fragment test, keep the tests for a credential as a whole number (nested and in arrays), for unrelated numbers unchanged, and for a too-large all-digit credential redacted as a string. Report one before-and-after timing at the size above in the PR. Run only test/credential-redaction.test.ts, `bunx biome check` on the changed files and `bunx tsc --noEmit`.

original.title: Restart deletes retained directories when no process identity was recorded
original.detail: Thank you: the per-job scope, the worker store, retention and recovery were reviewed and the tests pass in both environments. One gap in the new retention, reproduced by Codex: if process discovery fails before the first identity is recorded, `worker.cleanups` keeps the job's directories but `process_cleanups` has no row for the job. At the next start `recoverProcessCleanups` has nothing to confirm, so the retained directories are deleted while a detached descendant is still alive. Required: a retained job is deleted only after positive confirmation that its processes are gone. For example, record an unresolved marker for the job (its run id or scope marker) when it is retained, and at start confirm termination for that marker with the same discovery the scope uses. If confirmation fails or discovery is unavailable, keep the directories and the record, and refuse new jobs that would reuse them. original.title: An empty scan without the invocation's discovery record must not confirm a kept job; wait for a changed boot instead
original.detail:
Thank you: requirements (1) and (3) of the last round hold, and two kept jobs stay independent. The remaining gap is in requirement (2) as we wrote it last round. We asked for confirmation by "a successful scan for that job's marker that finds no live processes", and that was too permissive on our side: when the worker stopped after starting a process but before saving that invocation's discovery record, recovery scans with the fallback context from client.ts:290 (group 0, leader null), and an empty result there proves nothing. Reproduced against fdba89f0 through runWorker on macOS: a marked /bin/sh changes directory outside the job's roots and execs /bin/sleep, its launcher exits, the kept entry has no post-spawn discovery record, and after a restart the sleeper is still running while the job's root and scratch were removed. The same state follows a failed discovery save and any later worker death, not only a kill in the microseconds between spawn and save.

Required (this is the only new mechanism; keep everything else as round 2 made it):
1. Record each invocation as pending before it spawns. Pass the invocation marker (already created in startProcess before `beforeSpawn` runs) to `beforeSpawn`, and save it in the kept entry's pending set in the same save that `beforeSpawn` already does. Use a set, not a flag, so concurrent invocations within one job are covered.
2. A pending marker is cleared when that invocation's discovery record is saved, or when the running worker itself confirms that invocation's termination (the point where its cleanup records are deleted today, with the live child handle).
3. At recovery (startup and later attempts), a kept entry with any pending marker that has no saved discovery record is confirmed only by a host boot identity different from the recorded one. A successful or empty scan does not confirm it. Keep its directories, log it as unresolved, and keep running other jobs, exactly as for other unresolved entries. If the entry has no recorded boot identity, record the current one at the first recovery attempt that can read it, so a later reboot can confirm it.
4. Do not key this on the leader being null: on Linux the leader is always null, and recovery with saved discovery records must keep working there as it does now.
5. The `confirmed` field is only ever assigned `false` and never read; the pending set may replace it.

Tests (they must fail on fdba89f0, and the first two must run on Linux):
- A kept entry with a pending marker and no discovery record, an injected discover that returns [], and a restart: the directories and the entry are kept and the unresolved state is logged. Then a restart with a different boot identity removes them.
- An invocation whose discovery record is saved normally leaves no pending marker, and a normal job still removes everything at job end.
- Optionally, a macOS-only test of the /bin/sh -> cd outside -> exec /bin/sleep case above.
If an existing test such as "worker retries a job with failed boot inspection on a later heartbeat" conflicts with rule 3, keep rule 3 and say in your report which test changed and why. Run only the affected test files.

original.title: Check everything the push publishes: the full range from the remote head or base, and the branch name
original.detail: Thank you: token handling, confinement of repo.git (not writable by either harness's session) and the lease all held up in review. Two publication gaps remain, both reproduced against a local remote. (a) Only `parentSha..sha` is scanned, but pushing `sha` also publishes every ancestor the remote doesn't have. A private string in the parent's commit message reached the remote with `expectedRemoteSha: null`. (b) The branch name is published without any check. A push to `limitless/<private string>` succeeded with that string on the list and `discreet: true`. The coordinator's delivery (src/pipeline/engine.ts around line 2270) checks both; the worker must do the same, reusing the same functions rather than new ones. Required: (1) Add `baseSha` (the run's base commit) to `AgentJobRequest`, the lease projection and the worker schema, additively like the other publication fields. (2) Before the push, check the branch name with `checkPublicationText(branch, "Branch name", entries)`. (3) Compute the range with `publicationRange(cwd, baseSha, sha, expectedRemoteSha)` from src/git/repos.ts, which the coordinator uses, and run `checkPrivateRange`, the registered-credential check and (in discreet mode) `checkDiscreetCommits` on that range instead of `parentSha..sha`. If `expectedRemoteSha` is not present in the job's repository, refuse (the coordinator must send it in the bundle; that is S5's job). (4) In discreet mode, refuse an unpublished factory-marked branch name (starts with `limitless/` or contains the run id, with `expectedRemoteSha` null), the same rule as `deliveryPublicationRange` (src/git/repos.ts around line 989). Move that rule into one small shared helper that both `deliveryPublicationRange` and the worker call, so the two can't drift; don't change the coordinator's behaviour otherwise. Tests: a private string in an ancestor's message, in an ancestor's diff, and in the branch name each refuse with no push; a factory-marked unpublished branch in discreet mode refuses; a branch whose remote head is an ancestor scans only from that head.

original.title: Keep agentEnv()'s git config entries when adding the push's auth header
original.detail: The push environment spreads `agentEnv()` and then sets `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=1`, which drops `agentEnv()`'s own `credential.helper=` (and `diff.autoRefreshIndex`) entries. On a 401, git then consults the user's configured credential helper (confirmed with a loopback remote; the request still carried the header, but the helper must not be consulted at all). Required: append `http.extraHeader` after the entries `agentEnv()` already sets (read its `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`, add the header at the next index and increase the count) instead of replacing them. Test: the push's effective config (`git config --show-origin --get-all credential.helper` under the same environment, or an equivalent check) ends with the empty helper, and the header is still present.

original.title: Record the intended delivery push before pushing, and reconcile it on resume

original.title: Make adoption's only change a single reset, with the caller's signal
original.detail: `adoptWorkerCommit` ends with `resetTo(cwd, sha)`, which runs `git reset --hard` and then `git clean -fdq`, and doesn't take the signal. If the reset succeeds and the clean then fails (for example a confinement or preparation failure), the helper throws while HEAD already points to the worker commit, which breaks its "HEAD unchanged on refusal" contract. A cancel during that step is also ignored. Adoption has already verified that the worktree is clean, untracked files included, so the clean step is unnecessary there. Required: end adoption with one `worktreeGit(["git", "reset", "--hard", "-q", sha], { cwd, signal })` instead of `resetTo`, and leave `resetTo` unchanged for its other callers. Test: an injected failure of any step after the checks either leaves HEAD at the parent or the helper succeeds; a cancel before the reset leaves HEAD at the parent. No change is needed for writers racing adoption: the run's own engine is the only writer of its worktree, and it is awaiting the adoption.

original.title: Source mode must never take a build identity; packaged means a standalone executable
original.detail: Thank you: the resolver, the version command and the config builder's autoload options all checked out, and a binary built in scratch reported the right identity and ignored environment overrides. original.title: A cancel while an attempt is starting must stop it
original.detail: Thank you: the cancellation helper and the merge with #747 and #751 held up in review. One ordering gap remains. The scheduler calls `executeRun` (line 129) before it registers the run's controller (line 142). The engine publishes `running` synchronously, so a cancel arriving in that window (for example from a store subscriber on that first `running` publication) finds no controller, finalizes the cancel without aborting the execution, and delivery continues. Reproduced by resuming a due parked run with a one-shot subscriber that calls `scheduler.cancel` on its first `running` publication. Required: register the run's controller before execution starts, so `cancel` always reaches the running attempt. If an attempt starts and its cancel mark is already recorded, the existing `finalizeRecordedCancellation` check at entry stops it. Test: that subscriber-driven cancel stops the attempt before any delivery call, and the run ends cancelled.

original.title: Startup recovery reconciles cancel-marked queued rows
original.detail: Startup recovery looks only at `running` and `waiting_input` runs, and queue selection skips runs whose GitHub retry is in the future. So a queued run with `error: "cancelled by …"` and a future `githubWait.nextAttemptAt` (a crash between the cancel and the slot-release finalization) stays unfinalized until its retry is due, and an already-cancelled row that kept `githubWait` is never cleaned. Required: at startup, apply `finalizeRecordedCancellation` to every queued run that carries the cancel mark, and clear `githubWait` from cancelled runs, whatever their retry time. Test: both rows are reconciled at startup without waiting for admission or the retry time.

original.title: A failing runs-history request must not block the worker cards
original.detail: The page loads `/api/workers` and `/api/workers/runs` with one `Promise.all`, so a failure of the history request throws away a successful workers response. Against an older daemon (after a rollback), the history endpoint returns 404: the first load stays at "loading…" with an error, and later refreshes never update the cards. Required: apply each response on its own, each guarded by its own request generation. Show the history section as unavailable when its request fails, and keep refreshing the workers. Test: with `/api/workers/runs` answering 404, the cards render and refresh, and the history section says it is unavailable.

original.title: Keep local panel finders local when the run pins review models
original.detail: Thank you: eligibility, request shape, result validation, fallback, cancellation without a durable handle, the worker refusal and the result route all held up in review, and the new tests fail without the change. One gap against the issue's "What stays local: ... local finders". A panel finder with `local: true` is routed with `billing: "free_only"`, but when the run pins `run.models.review` the pinned chain overrides that and resolves a subscription CLI target with no `backend`/`openai`/`decisions`. The call still receives `checkout`, so the executor sends it to a worker. Reproduced through the real panel test with a preload probe: constraint "free_only", target billing "subscription", and a done review row in `agent_jobs`. Required: a local finder's call never carries `checkout`, so it always runs local(); decide this from the finder (or the `free_only` constraint) at the review call site, not from the resolved target. Test: extend the panel test so a local finder with a pinned review chain creates no `agent_jobs` row while the other finders still go to the worker.

original.title: Keep Babel out of the binary with the define checked in ui.ts (option 1)
original.detail: Thank you for stopping and reporting this with a probe: it is the right call, and the shared UI options, staging, embedding, the packaged loader and `validateMetafile` all stay as they are. Decision: take your option 1. Bun 1.4.3 removes a dynamic import only when the build define is tested in the same module, so `src/server/ui.ts` tests the release define directly, next to the `await import("../../scripts/solid-plugin.ts")`, with a short comment saying why the check can't live in `src/release.ts` (a constant exported from another module isn't folded). This supersedes the issue's "don't reference the define in ui.ts" and H-3's objection; it adds no second install-kind mechanism, because `release.ts` stays the only place that decides the install kind at runtime. Keep `validateMetafile` as the real check (a binary whose metafile has any `@babel/` or `babel-preset-solid` input is refused and deleted). Restore the test you removed from `test/ui-build.test.ts` that bundles `ui.ts` with the define set and asserts no Babel input remains; it must fail without the in-module check. Report the real build probe's output again (metafile Babel inputs: 0, binary size vs 80,654,066 bytes). Run only the affected test files, `bunx biome check` and `bunx tsc --noEmit`: never the full suite in a factory run (AGENTS.md); its environment failures are expected inside the sandbox.

original.title: Source mode must not act on a foreign LIMITLESS_BUILD_PACKAGED
original.detail: Thank you: the probe confirms the goal. A release build has 0 Babel inputs (1,149 total; the binary is 77,170,034 bytes against 80,654,066), the embedded UI matches the source build's keys, bytes and content types, and staging leaves exactly the build outputs. One gap of the same class as #759's identity defines was reproduced. In source mode, `[define] LIMITLESS_BUILD_PACKAGED = "true"` in a `bunfig.toml` in the caller's directory, or `globalThis.LIMITLESS_BUILD_PACKAGED = true` set at runtime, makes `buildUi()` skip the Solid build. It then throws `Packaged Limitless is missing its embedded UI or index.html`, although `release.kind` is still `source`. Required: keep the in-module define check, so Bun still drops the plugin import in release builds, but decide by `info.kind` first. A `source` release with the define set must not take the packaged path. Either build normally, or refuse with a message that names the define and where it came from; don't report a missing embedded UI. Tests: in source mode, a caller `bunfig.toml` `[define]` and a runtime global each produce the source behaviour you chose (spawn `bun` from another directory, as test/version-cli.test.ts does for the identity defines).
