original.title: An interrupt during the drain request can leave the daemon draining
original.detail: Thank you: the restart flow, the boot check and the docs all look right. One ordering problem remains, shown by an orchestrator probe with an injected deferred drain request. (1) `requestAdmin(client, clock, "drain")` is sent and is still pending. (2) SIGINT arrives, and `race` rejects at once. (3) The cleanup path sends `resume`, the restart exits non-zero and releases the lock. (4) The original drain request is then applied by the daemon, so it stays `draining: true` with nobody left to resume it. The interrupt test at test/restart.test.ts:167 applies the drain before emitting the signal, so it misses this order. Fix: keep the drain request's promise, and on an interrupt wait for it to settle (bounded by the existing request timeout) before deciding whether to resume, so a resume is never sent ahead of a drain still in flight. Deploy's own drain at line 694 and service install's at line 368 race the same way, so put the fix in one shared place that all three use rather than three copies (AGENTS.md: one guard, every path). Add a test with a drain request that resolves only after the interrupt: the final state is not draining, resume is sent after the drain applied, and no kickstart happens. Run it for restart and for deploy. It must fail without the fix. Run only the affected test files (test/restart.test.ts test/deploy.test.ts test/deploy-process.test.ts test/drain-http.test.ts test/service.test.ts), `bunx biome check` on the changed files and `bunx tsc --noEmit`. Never run the full suite in a factory run (AGENTS.md).

original.title: A live owner's held slot expires during an event-loop stall, so two holders run at limit 1
original.detail: Thank you: the transactions, priority order and the shared limit all work, and two simultaneously started processes never over-admitted. The problem is expiry. `refresh()` deletes rows whose `renewed_at` is older than `GATE_LEASE_EXPIRY_MS`, and a process renews its own rows only from its 250 ms pulse at the 10 s renewal interval. An orchestrator probe: A acquires at t=0, B queues at t=9 s, A's event loop stalls for 22 s (a long synchronous step or a busy SQLite wait), and B's refresh at t=31 s deletes A's held row and admits B. A's `acquire()` already resolved, so A's gate keeps running with no notice: two full suites at limit 1, which the issue forbids ("held slots are never interrupted"). All processes sharing this database run on the same machine, so tie in-process holders to the owning process, not to a timestamp. Record the owner's pid and process start time with the owner id. A row is expired when its owning process is gone (no such pid, or a different start time), checked inside the admission transaction. Keep the time-based expiry only for external leases (`lease_until`, renewed by the `gate-slot` client's heartbeat), whose owner is the client. Add a test with an injected clock and an injected liveness check: an owner that stops renewing but is still alive keeps its held slot, and a waiter elsewhere gets it only once the owner is reported gone.

original.title: A waiting external lease loses its queue position across a daemon restart
original.detail: `heartbeat()` returns undefined for a row owned by another owner unless it is held, and release does the same. A probe: a `gate-slot` client waits in the queue, the daemon restarts (new owner id), and the client's next heartbeat and release both return undefined. The client then re-requests (its existing behaviour), the abandoned original row is admitted later and holds capacity until it expires, while the replacement waits. The issue asks that "a daemon restart doesn't forget a live external holder"; a waiting lease needs the same. A lease id is the client's capability, so let `heartbeat` adopt a waiting row as it adopts a held one (set the new owner, renew `lease_until`, re-arm the expiry), and let a release with that id delete the row whatever its owner. Test: a waiting external lease survives a restart with its position, then is admitted in order, and its release frees the row.

original.title: Idle pools run a write transaction every 250 ms
original.detail: Each pool's pulse runs `refresh()`, a `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction, every 250 ms whether or not anything waits. Measured: two idle pools ran 79 transactions in 10 s, and an idle poll blocked the event loop for 601 ms while another process held the write lock for 600 ms. bun:sqlite is synchronous and the store sets `busy_timeout = 5000`, so a longer hold elsewhere stalls the daemon for up to 5 s, and with the stall above that feeds expiry. Poll only while this process has a local waiter. Renew this process's own rows at the renewal interval only when it owns any. Run no transaction when idle. Wake same-process waiters on release, as now. Test with an injected timer: an idle pool schedules no transactions, and a waiter's polling stops once it is admitted or aborted. Run only the affected test files (test/gate-slots-db.test.ts test/gate-slot.test.ts test/gate-slot-http.test.ts test/agent-test-session.test.ts test/gates.test.ts), `bunx biome check` on the changed files and `bunx tsc --noEmit`. Never run the full suite in a factory run (AGENTS.md).

original.title: A refusal event from a newer worker aborts the session on an older coordinator
original.detail: Thank you: the lanes, roles, policy provenance and the bypass paths all held up under probing (`bun run test`, `bunx bun test` and `env bun test` all reached the wrapper and were refused). One compatibility problem remains. The refusal is reported as a `status` event with a new `data` field, and the agent-event schema is strict. A job leased before a deploy rollback keeps running on its worker. An orchestrator probe against origin/main's listener: a plain status event returned 200, and the new refusal event returned HTTP 400, after which the newer worker aborted its active session. AGENTS.md requires the previous release to keep working across a rollback. Keep the event shape unchanged instead: report the refusal as an ordinary `status` event whose text carries the redacted command, for example `agent-test refused: full suite: bun test --parallel=4`, and drop the new `data` field and its schema change. Update the tests to match, and keep one that fails without the refusal event. Not required: jobs queued by an older coordinator before the upgrade reattach without the policy and behave as "slot" (today's default). That is acceptable; don't add migration code for it. Run only the affected test files (test/agent-test.test.ts test/agent-test-session.test.ts test/pipeline-slotted.test.ts test/pipeline-agent-executor.test.ts test/lan-agent.test.ts test/workers.test.ts), `bunx biome check` on the changed files and `bunx tsc --noEmit`. Never run the full suite in a factory run (AGENTS.md).

original.title: A land check can switch gate executors mid-check after a reload
original.detail: Thank you: the stage-scoped config, the executor capture in `invoke` and `runGateExecution`, the limits and the feed all held up under probing. The land queue reads `gateExecutor` through the new getter at each use, so a reload between a land check and its targeted retry (src/land/queue.ts:829) changes the executor mid-check. An orchestrator probe removed the repository from `workers.repos` during a LAN check. The retry then ran locally without the setup the LAN run had done, failed with `Cannot find package 'retry-dependency'`, and blocked the land. With the executor pinned for the whole check, the same scenario landed. Capture the executor once when a land entry's check starts, and use it for every check, retry and cancellation of that attempt, as `runGateExecution` does for a stage. The next land entry uses the reloaded one. Test: a reload that changes the gate executor between a land check and its retry keeps the original executor for the retry, and the next entry uses the new one.

original.title: Replacing a live table with a non-table value still applies part of it
original.detail: The requirement is "Every other changed key is listed as restartRequired and isn't applied, not even partly." An orchestrator probe started with run and gate limits 7 and 5, then replaced `[limits]` with `limits = 42`. Reload returned 200, listed `limits` in `restartRequired`, and still changed the active limits to the loader's defaults (3 and 4), along with `cfg.raw.limits`. A live key may apply only when its section is a table in both the current and the new config. When a section changes shape (added, removed, or replaced by a non-table), apply none of its keys, report it under `restartRequired`, and keep the current values and raw section. Test each live section (`workers`, `limits`, `review`) replaced by a scalar, and removed: the active values and `cfg.raw` are unchanged, and the section is listed as restart-required.

original.title: Switching the review mode mid-run makes the run fail on resume
original.detail: This one also reproduces on origin/main, but reload turns it from a restart-only case into one command: changing `[review] mode` now applies to stages that start later. original.title: The shared glob matcher admits paths outside the pattern
original.detail: Thank you: the diff edge cases, trusted configuration, the Python fallback, the land queue and verify substitution all held up under probing. Three problems remain, each in the direction of running fewer tests than the evidence claims. First: with `docs = ["docs/**/guide.md"]`, a change to only `docs/notguide.md` was treated as docs-only and the test check was skipped. The reused `globToRegex` (src/gates/audit.ts) lets `**/` match a partial name, so `docs/**/guide.md` matches `docs/notguide.md`. Fix the shared matcher, the one implementation, so `**/` matches zero or more whole directories and `*` never crosses a `/`. The protected-paths audit uses the same function, so it becomes exact too (today it can over-match, the safe direction). Add matcher tests: `docs/**/guide.md` matches `docs/guide.md` and `docs/a/b/guide.md` but not `docs/notguide.md` or `docsx/guide.md`; `*.md` matches only top-level Markdown files; `test/fixtures/**` keeps matching everything under it.

The live-owner guard also skips invocations that belong to this same process. Probe: a real subprocess with a temporary database, an invocation that exited while its shutdown scan was forced to fail. Its descendant survived and its discovery row remained. Recovery in a fresh scope in the same process then returned successfully, kept the orphan and the row, and let the next command run. Removing only this guard recovered both. Invocations that this process is still running are already excluded by `activeInvocations`. So skip a row for a live owner only when the owner is another process (its `ownerId` differs from this process's). For this process's own rows, keep today's rule: active invocations are left alone, and everything else is recovered. Add a test for exactly this probe, which must fail without the fix. Optional: cache this process's own identity once, since the measured per-spawn cost is noise either way. Run only test/process-cleanups.test.ts test/migrations.test.ts test/proc.test.ts, `bunx biome check` on the changed files and `bunx tsc --noEmit`. Never run the full suite in a factory run (AGENTS.md).

original.title: Gate mode must work with the LAN gate executor, which this installation uses
original.detail: Thank you: snapshot/commit equality, exact reuse, preserved failure feedback, verify substitution, priority, cancellation, the migration and the "slot"/"refuse" modes all held in review. One gap defeats the issue's goal in production. The session handler is offered only when the gate executor is absent or `kind === "local"` (src/pipeline/context.ts:923), and `reusableAgentGate` returns null for any other executor (src/pipeline/agent-gate.ts:92). This installation runs `[gates] executor = "lan"`, so with `agent_full_suite = "gate"` the request is refused, no record is created, and the gates stage runs the full suite again: the feature does nothing. The existing `lan` integration case confirms this. The issue requires the normal gate executor, and "local implement sessions only" limits which sessions get the mode, not which executor runs the gate. LAN gate jobs already run from git bundles at a requested commit, so the snapshot commit can go through `executeGate` with `ctx.deps.gateExecutor` exactly like a gates-stage run (same request shape, the same base-commit test check, gate environment and `start` priority). Record and reuse the result the same way for both executors, so the gates stage reuses a LAN execution for the same tree, gate configuration and environment. If a worker infrastructure failure falls back to running locally, that is still a factory gate execution and is recorded as usual. Tests: with a fake LAN gate executor, (a) a session request runs the gate through that executor and records it; (b) the gates stage then reuses it and runs nothing; (c) a different tree still runs normally. Each must fail without the fix. Run only test/agent-full-suite-gate.test.ts test/agent-test.test.ts test/gate-evidence.test.ts test/lan-agent.test.ts test/pipeline-slotted.test.ts, `bunx biome check` on the changed files and `bunx tsc --noEmit`. Never run the full suite in a factory run (AGENTS.md).

original.title: A repeated request for an unchanged tree should reuse the recorded execution
original.detail: Each wrapper request gets a fresh request ID (src/cli/agent-test.ts:210), and `runAgentGate` executes without looking up an existing record (src/pipeline/agent-gate.ts:158). The request-serialization test shows two requests for the same tree invoking the handler twice, so an implementer that runs the full suite three times on one tree waits for three gate executions. Before executing, look up the record by the same key the gates stage uses (run, tree, gate configuration, environment). If one exists, return its result, failure and feedback unchanged, with output saying it was reused; otherwise run as today. Use one lookup implementation for both callers, not a copy. Test: two requests for the same tree run the gate once and both return the same result; a request after a file change runs again. It must fail without the fix.

original.title: Select the default branch's historical commit along first-parent history
original.detail: Thank you: write filtering, id allocation, idempotent re-runs, Biome formatting, validation exclusions and worktree cleanup all held in review, and a read-only preview against the real database produced 121 proposed cases with no private-string matches. One base-selection case is wrong. `git rev-list -1 --before=<seconds> <default branch>` walks every parent, so a topic branch merged into the default branch after the round can supply the selected commit. Probe: topic head H merged historical main commit M; after the review, the topic was merged into main with a merge commit. The timestamp-filtered walk selected H from the later merge's second-parent history, and the generator accepted base === head === H, an empty review diff, instead of base M. Add `--first-parent` so only commits that were on the default branch itself are considered, and reject a case whose base equals its head ("empty diff"). Test: exactly this history (real git) selects M with the fix and fails without it.

original.title: Any finished issue run requires re-approval, not only failed or cancelled ones
original.detail: Thank you: the transactional claim held on every start path (queue, webhook, comments, MCP, HTTP/CLI, chat, retries), review/conflict/CI rounds still insert, label re-application, null actors, login casing, ordering and the off-by-default paths all held in review. The re-pick rule is too narrow. Probe with `issueEligibility` (open issue, trusted author, priority:1 applied by the owner before the run): the latest issue-sourced run `succeeded` and its closing PR was closed without merging → eligible; latest run `succeeded` with no PR → eligible; latest run `resolved` with no PR → eligible; closing PR `MERGED` but the issue still open → eligible. Each starts a new run of work the owner rejected or that already finished, on every poll. Rule: when the issue has any earlier issue-sourced run that is no longer active, it is eligible only if a trusted account applied a priority label after that latest run finished (`finishedAt`; missing counts as not finished). This keeps the failure rule and covers the rest; the normal path is unaffected (an open PR excludes the issue, a merged PR closes it). Update docs/ISSUES.md. Tests: the four cases above are ineligible until a trusted priority label is applied after the run finished, then eligible; each fails without the fix.

original.title: Body blocker lines in other shapes must not be ignored
original.detail: Only an exact `Blocked by #n` line is recognised, so other shapes fail open. Probe (body blocker #12 open, #13 open): `Blocked by #12, #13`, `- Blocked by #12` and `Blocked by: #12` are each eligible; only `Blocked by #12` is excluded. Treat every `#n` on any line whose text (after optional whitespace and a list marker such as `-`, `*` or `1.`) starts with `blocked by` (case-insensitive, optional colon) as a blocker. Keep docs/ISSUES.md's one-per-line advice, and say that other shapes on such a line still count. Tests: the three shapes are excluded while a named issue is open and eligible once all are closed; each fails without the fix.

original.title: An untrusted title rename must make the issue ineligible
original.detail: The title is part of the run request (`issueRunRequest` quotes title and body), but only the body editor is checked. Probe: a trusted, approved issue whose title was renamed by an untrusted account stays eligible and its run quotes the new title. Read `RENAMED_TITLE_EVENT` items in the same timeline query (`... on RenamedTitleEvent { actor { login } createdAt }`) and exclude the issue when the most recent rename's actor is untrusted or missing ("untrusted title editor"). Keep the 100-item window rule: a rename outside the window that can't be seen doesn't approve anything, so if the timeline connection is incomplete, the issue is ineligible ("incomplete issue evidence"). Tests: untrusted rename → excluded; trusted rename → eligible; each fails without the fix.

original.title: Claims for issue-sourced runs come from the source reference, not from quoted issue text
original.detail: `closedIssues(req.prompt)` scans the whole prompt, including the quoted issue body. Probe: starting a run for issue #1 whose body contains `> Closes #2` claims #2, and a genuine start for #2 is then refused as claimed by #1's run (also with the queue disabled). For a request whose `sourceRef.kind` is `issue`, claim only `sourceRef`; parse `Closes #n` directives only from prompts that aren't quoted GitHub text (requests whose `source` isn't `github`). `issueClaim` must apply the same rule to existing runs, so an active issue run never claims a number mentioned in its quoted body. Tests: the probe above lets #2 start, and `limitless run` with `Closes #2` still claims #2; each fails without the fix.

original.title: Re-check admission (limits, draining, stop) with no await before the insert
original.detail: Capacity, the issue-run limit and draining are checked, then `factory.createRun` awaits repository resolution before inserting (check-then-act across an await, AGENTS.md). Probes with state changed at that await: two queued runs with `max_concurrent_runs = 1`; two active issue runs with `max_issue_runs = 1`; a run queued after the scheduler started draining; and a run inserted after `stop()` returned. Pass an admission predicate through `createRun` to `Store.createRun` and evaluate it inside the same transaction as the claim check and the insert (counts of active runs and issue runs, `scheduler.draining`, the queue's `stopped` flag). A refused admission returns without creating a run and is logged. Only the queue passes a predicate; other callers are unchanged. Tests: each of the four probes creates no run with the fix and fails without it.

original.title: Clamp the poll timer for far-future rate-limit resets
original.detail: `set(tick, Math.max(pollSeconds * 1000, notBefore - now()))` passes a delay above setTimeout's 2^31-1 ms limit when `resetAt` is far in the future. Probe: low remaining budget with a reset 40 days ahead makes Bun warn and fire after 1 ms, five callbacks in 6 ms, a busy loop until the reset. Cap each timer at one hour while keeping `notBefore` as the absolute deadline (ticks before it query nothing, as today). Test: a far-future reset schedules the next tick at the cap, not at 1 ms; it fails without the fix.

original.title: The tests must pass inside confined gates: don't canonicalize this checkout's repository from the tests
original.detail: Thank you: all three round-1 fixes held in review (first-parent base, acceptance-only dedupe, redacted validation fields), and the tests fail without them. The land check then blocked with 25 failures in test/review-escape-cases.test.ts, and the orchestrator reproduced them by running the file inside the real gate profile (Seatbelt, home read-denied, gate environment) from a checkout under the home: every case that calls `reviewEscapeCases` fails with `Cannot read private-strings.txt; publication blocked`. The tests' own temporary `LIMITLESS_CONFIG_DIR` is fine. The cause is `loadPrivateStrings(undefined, [resolve(import.meta.dir, "..")])`: `readPrivateStrings` canonicalizes the given repository root, its common directory and every linked checkout listed under `worktrees/`. Inside a gate, the other runs' checkouts are unreadable, so the call fails, and whether it fails depends on which other worktrees happen to exist (the run's own gate classified it as flaky). Make the repository roots for the private-strings check an option of `reviewEscapeCases` (default: this checkout, as today, so the CLI's behaviour is unchanged) and pass the fixture repository from the tests, so nothing outside the test's temporary directory is canonicalized. Keep everything else the tests read inside their temporary directory too (AGENTS.md, "The home is read-denied for gates", #500). The factory's gates run confined and will show whether this holds; don't add retries. Run only test/review-escape-cases.test.ts test/evals-cases.test.ts, `bunx biome check` on the changed files and `bunx tsc --noEmit`. Never run the full suite in a factory run (AGENTS.md).

The land check then blocked with 25 failures in test/review-escape-cases.test.ts, and the orchestrator reproduced them by running the file inside the real gate profile (Seatbelt, home read-denied, gate environment) from a checkout under the home: every case that calls `reviewEscapeCases` fails with `Cannot read private-strings.txt; publication blocked`. The tests' own temporary `LIMITLESS_CONFIG_DIR` is fine. The cause is `loadPrivateStrings(undefined, [resolve(import.meta.dir, "..")])`: `readPrivateStrings` canonicalizes the given repository root, its common directory and every linked checkout listed under `worktrees/`. Inside a gate, the other runs' checkouts are unreadable, so the call fails, and whether it fails depends on which other worktrees happen to exist (the run's own gate classified it as flaky). Make the repository roots for the private-strings check an option of `reviewEscapeCases` (default: this checkout, as today, so the CLI's behaviour is unchanged) and pass the fixture repository from the tests, so nothing outside the test's temporary directory is canonicalized. Keep everything else the tests read inside their temporary directory too (AGENTS.md, "The home is read-denied for gates", #500). The factory's gates run confined and will show whether this holds; don't add retries. original.title: Record session-gate evidence only when the snapshot is still at the commit the gate ran on
original.detail: The factory's own review in the conflict round found this, and it is right. `runAgentGate` runs PR-controlled test code in the snapshot checkout (a standalone repository created by `exportGateSnapshot` in scratch, whose `.git` is inside the write roots), then stores the result with `putAgentGate` under the original `tree`. A test that commits in the snapshot (for example `git commit -am x` or `git reset --hard <other>` and then exit 0) leaves HEAD at a different commit, but the result is still recorded as evidence for the original tree, suppresses the round's own test run, and can satisfy verify's substitution. The gates stage already guards against exactly this (src/pipeline/engine.ts around line 1651: "A gate may have changed HEAD itself; those results cannot attest to the checked commit"; evidence is recorded only when `headSha(cwd) === checkedSha`). Apply the same rule here: after the execution and any retries, re-read the snapshot checkout's HEAD and HEAD's tree, and call `putAgentGate` only if HEAD still equals `head` (captured before the run) and its tree equals `tree`. Otherwise record nothing, still return the result to the session, and add a line to its output saying the result is not reusable because the snapshot changed during the gate. For the LAN executor, check the same thing on what the worker reports for the executed commit, if it reports one; if the provenance can't be confirmed, don't record (fail closed). Tests (each must fail without the fix): (a) a test command that commits in the snapshot and exits 0 → no record, the gates stage runs the test check, and verify does not substitute it; (b) a test command that resets HEAD to another commit → no record; (c) the unchanged-HEAD case still records and reuses. original.title: Match process records by canonical path when confirming a worktree's job stopped
original.detail: Thank you: release identity, slot ownership across restarts and fallback, idle-read-only polling, atomic leasing, LAN/in-place separation, default-off behaviour, older-config acceptance and the additive migration all held in review, and the new tests fail without the change. One path bug undermines the worktree lock. `waitStopped` and the executor's own `stopped` check query process discoveries and cleanups with the request's `cwd` spelling, but discovery rows store canonical paths. Probe on macOS (/var → /private/var): one discovery row exists, but zero match the request's spelling; after the executor was killed, fallback ran while the original check was still alive, and the job was marked `stopped=1`. Canonicalize (`realpathSync`, the same way discovery records it) before every match, in `waitStopped`, the executor's `finally`, and the `start()` scan for earlier jobs in the same worktree. This is also what makes the three symlink-sensitive tests in test/gate-inplace-executor.test.ts fail on macOS unconfined runs and on Linux CI (`shutdown detaches and a new context reattaches…`, `executor crash recovery during/before resume…`). Test: a request cwd given through a symlink is still confirmed stopped only after its process is gone; it fails without the fix.

original.title: Use the daemon's current port for each job's confinement, not the executor's startup config
original.detail: The executor builds its Seatbelt backend once from its startup `cfg.port`. After a same-release daemon restart on a different port, it still leases jobs but its profile denies only the old port. Probe: under the daemon's profile `curl` to the daemon port exits 7; through the executor it exits 0 and receives the response. Put the daemon's port in the job request (the daemon fills it from its own config, like `env` and `releaseSha`), and build the job's confinement with `seatbeltForPort(req.daemonPort)`; refuse a job without one. Test: an executor started with one port runs a job whose request names another, and the job's profile denies the request's port; it fails without the fix.

original.title: Every wait for an in-place job to stop must end
original.detail: `waitStopped` recovers processes only when the executor's process identity is gone; while the executor is alive it sleeps and re-checks forever. Probe: a suspended (alive but stuck) executor whose lease expired leaves the job `failed` with `stopped=0`, and `waitStopped` never returns; a failed cleanup in the executor's `finally` leaves the same state. Keep the worktree lock, but bound the wait: once the lease has expired and a grace period (for example two lease periods) has passed with `stopped=0`, stop waiting and fail the gate with a confinement/operational error naming the job and saying process recovery is required, so the run surfaces it (needs_human) instead of hanging. Never signal the executor itself. Tests: a stuck executor (lease expired, process alive, `stopped=0`) and a failed cleanup each end with that error within the bound; each fails without the fix.

original.title: Retries through the executor must see the setup's scratch, as in-process retries do
original.detail: Each job's `executeGate` creates and removes its own command scratch, and retries skip setup because the executor reports no fresh checkout. Probe: setup writes `$HOME/setup-token` (HOME is the scratch); the retry passes in-process (exit 0) and fails through the executor (exit 1). Make a retry job reuse the scratch of the attempt it retries (the daemon passes the same scratch identity in the request, and the executor keeps that scratch until the retry chain ends), or run setup again for executor retries. Test: exactly this probe passes through the executor; it fails without the fix.

original.title: Restore committed bytes before an in-process fallback after an executor failure

original.title: Exempt only the outer profile, and only keychain paths that aren't another credential store
original.detail:
Thank you. The orchestrator checked the generated profiles directly with `codex sandbox`, with no model involved:
- On main, an unconfined Codex reader can list ~/.ssh, ~/.config/limitless, ~/.config/gh, ~/.codex and ~/Library/Keychains, and a Codex editor can query the keychain.
- With this change all of these are denied, for unconfined and confined readers and for editors, and the checkout stays readable.
- Review also found every session path covered on both backends and on LAN workers, the probe fail-closed and cached per profile, and no canaries in credential stores. The tests fail without the change.

Two gaps remain in the Claude editor exemption.

(1) `claudeEditorRoots` removes every keychain spelling from `denyRead`, so a keychain path that is also the spelling of another required deny loses that deny too. Probe: in a synthetic home where `Library/Keychains` is a symlink to `.ssh`, the shared policy denies `.ssh`, but the editor profile omits it. A real Seatbelt listing of `.ssh` exits 1 before the alias and 0 after. Remove a keychain spelling only when it isn't also a spelling of another entry in the credential list; if they overlap, keep the deny (fail closed).

(2) The same exempted roots also build the editor's native-tool rules (`Read(...)` in `permissions.deny` and `--disallowedTools`, src/harness/claude.ts around line 204), so the editor's native Read, Grep and Glob can read ~/Library/Keychains. The CLI reads its own login through `security`, not through its Read tool. Build the native rules from the full deny list, including the keychain, and use the exempted list only for the outer Seatbelt profile (`runSandboxed`'s roots).

Tests, each of which must fail without the fix:
- with the keychain aliased to `.ssh`, the editor's outer profile still denies `.ssh`;
- a Claude editor's `permissions.deny` and `--disallowedTools` contain `Read(...)` rules for every keychain spelling, while its outer profile allows them.

Run only test/harness.test.ts test/scratch.test.ts test/smoke.test.ts test/failure-injection.test.ts test/sandbox.test.ts, `bunx biome check` on the changed files and `bunx tsc --noEmit`. Never run the full suite in a factory run (AGENTS.md).

original.title: Protect the App private key from agent and gate reads, at the daemon's startup
original.detail: Thank you: the call-site inventory came back clean in review. Every factory GitHub call for a listed repository goes through the provider; the JWT and token are registered before use and never reach agents, gates or workers; login comparisons (approval gate, mergedBy, comment markers, fork checks, Dependabot, queue trust) keep their meaning; the discreet-mode refusal and doctor output hold; the tests fail without the change. The factory's own review found this one and it is right: `private_key_path` may point outside the config directory, and agents run as the same user, so mode 0600 doesn't stop them. Register the key exactly the way the daemon registers its other private files: in `startScopedDaemon` (src/cli/daemon.ts, next to the `worker-tls`/`worker` loop that calls `protectPrivateFile(join(home, file))`), when `factory.cfg.githubApp` is set, push `protectPrivateFile(factory.cfg.githubApp.privateKeyPath)` onto `privateFiles` before the listener, integrations or any run starts, so it is released on shutdown with the others. `protectPrivateFile` already covers the configured and canonical spellings (including a symlink's target). If config reload (#807) can change `[github.app]`, protect the new path before switching and release the old one after. Tests (each must fail without the fix): with `[github.app]` configured and the key at an absolute path outside the config directory, `privateReadPaths()` contains it and its canonical spelling after startup; a symlinked key path protects both the link and its target; an agent's `denyRead` (for example `validateDenyRead` / `homeReadPolicy`) includes the key.

original.title: Never let a flag's value select the identity: pass the known repository explicitly
original.detail: `githubRepo` scans argument values, so a value that looks like a flag changes the selection. Probe: for a listed repository `o/r`, a PR body of exactly `--repo` makes `mergePullRequest` (src/git/repos.ts) run `gh pr merge https://github.com/o/r/pull/1 --squash --delete-branch --subject "change (#1)" --body "--repo" --match-head-commit <sha>`; `githubRepo` returns `--match-head-commit`, the provider selects `owner`, and the merge runs with the owner's login, while the PR lookup just before it used the App token. A listed repository must never silently run as the owner. Fix both ways: every factory helper that knows its repository passes it to `githubSh` explicitly (the merge, PR creation/edit/view helpers in src/git/repos.ts, the notifier, the engine's comment helpers), and `githubRepo` only reads `--repo`/`-R` values and positional arguments, skipping the value of every other flag that takes one (`--body`, `--subject`, `--title`, `-f`, `-F`, `--field`, `--raw-field`, `--jq`, `--match-head-commit`, …). Also fail closed: when a call's explicit repository and the repository parsed from a PR URL argument disagree, refuse the call. Tests (each must fail without the fix): exactly the probe above runs with the App token; a `--body`/`-f body=` value containing `--repo x/y` or a URL of another repository doesn't change the selection.

original.title: Validate the key file at each signing, not only at config load
original.detail: The 0600 and regular-file checks run when the configuration loads (src/config.ts), but signing reads the file again with `readFileSync`. Probes: a key loaded at 0600, exchanged once, then changed to 0644, is still used at token refresh; a configured symlink to a 0600 key is accepted because `statSync` follows it. At each signing, open the key with `O_NOFOLLOW` (or `lstat` first and refuse a symlink), `fstat` the opened descriptor, refuse anything that isn't a regular file owned by this user with no group or other permission bits, then read through that descriptor. original.title: Merge the default branch, and keep agent full-suite gates off the in-place executor
original.detail: Thank you: all five round-2 fixes held in review. Canonical-path stop confirmation, the request's daemon port (with a real Seatbelt denial), the bounded stop wait that survives renewed leases, setup scratch shared with executor retries, and the committed-byte restore before fallback all held. The tests pass normally and inside the real gate profile, and they fail without the round. The PR conflicts with the default branch again since #820, #835, #833 and #844 landed. Merge it and resolve the conflicts, keeping both sides' behaviour. The conflict round's own review found the integration problem this creates, and it is right. #820's `runAgentGate` (src/pipeline/agent-gate.ts) calls `executeGate` with the shared `ctx.deps.gateExecutor`. With `[executor] enabled`, that is now the in-place executor, but the request carries no `releaseSha`, `env` or `daemonPort`. `leaseInplace` requires a matching `releaseSha`, so the job can never be leased, and every agent full-suite request (and each retry) waits out the 60-second pickup timeout before falling back. Agent sessions are out of scope for this slice (E3). When the configured gate executor is in-place, run `runAgentGate` on the local in-process executor exactly as it runs today without the executor, and pass `freshCheckoutFor` and reuse the same way. Its LAN behaviour is unchanged. Test, which must fail without the fix: with `[executor] enabled` and a live executor, an agent full-suite request runs in-process immediately, with no in-place job row and no pickup wait, and the gates stage still reuses it.

original.title: Remove a detached run's retained scratch when the run is cancelled
original.detail: `gateCommandScope` keeps an in-place job's scratch across a daemon shutdown so a resumed stage can re-attach, but cancelling such a run never removes it. Probe: start a scoped gate, detach it with `shutdown`, then cancel the queued run. The run and job both end `cancelled`, the job has `stopped=1`, and the scratch directory still exists. When a run ends in a terminal state (cancel, failure, or a stage that starts over after a mismatch), remove the retained scratch once the job's processes are confirmed stopped (`waitStopped`), on the same path that cancels the job. original.title: Protect a reloaded App key path as soon as it is validated, not only at startup
original.detail:
Thank you: all three round-1 fixes held in review.
- Startup registers the key in both spellings, and real Seatbelt agent and gate probes deny reads of it, with an allowed-read control that succeeds.
- The `--repo` body, `-f body=--repo x/y` and a `--body` holding another repository's URL all keep the App token.
- At the next signing, a key that is 0644, symlinked, not a regular file or owned by another user fails closed with a clear reason and no key contents.
- The tests fail without the round.

One gap remains. When a config reload (#807) changes `[github.app] private_key_path`, the reload validates the new path and reports `restartRequired: ["github.app.private_key_path"]`, so the old key stays active and protected. The new path, though, is never registered with `protectPrivateFile`.

Probe: two synthetic 0600 keys outside the config directory. After the reload, the new path is absent from `privateReadPaths()`, and a fresh Seatbelt agent read probe can read the new key while the old one is denied.

Fix: register every validated `private_key_path` with `protectPrivateFile` as soon as the reload accepts it, before any agent or gate can start, and keep it registered until shutdown (the same `privateFiles` lifetime as the startup registration). A pending key is a credential too. Don't release the old key's protection while it is still the active key.

Test, which must fail without the fix: after a reload that changes the path, both the old and the new key paths, in both spellings, are in `privateReadPaths()`.

Optional, for consistency: pass the repository explicitly in the five remaining calls that still infer it. Review showed they select the App token correctly today. They are in src/pipeline/review-round.ts (the PR view near line 105, and the auto-merge cancellation near 205) and src/pipeline/shadow-report.ts (the three history calls near lines 44, 49 and 62).

Run only test/github-app.test.ts test/config-reload.test.ts test/github-notifier.test.ts, `bunx biome check` on the changed files and `bunx tsc --noEmit`. Never run the full suite in a factory run (AGENTS.md).

original.title: Apply the PID readiness wait to every test that reads a PID file, through one helper
Inspect tracked files through a fresh temporary index, so gate-set index flags can't hide a change
original.detail:
Thank you for the shared `gateProvenance` check; the approach is right. Rounds 3–5 never reached this finding: each implement session failed at startup with a Claude login error, so the code is unchanged since round 2.

The working-tree comparison trusts the checkout's own index. An index entry marked `assume-unchanged` or `skip-worktree` is skipped by both `git update-index --refresh` and `git diff --name-only <sha> --`. Review reproduced this in a temporary repository: after `git update-index --assume-unchanged tracked.txt` (or `--skip-worktree`) and a rewrite of tracked.txt, the check returned `paths: []` and `trackedClean: true` while the file held different bytes. An ordinary rewrite was correctly reported. Gate confinement normally prevents a gate from writing the index, but this check must not depend on that.

Fix: for the working-tree comparison, build a fresh temporary index from the checked commit and compare the checkout against it.
- Put the index file in a private temporary directory outside the checkout, and remove it afterwards.
- Run `worktreeGit` with `GIT_INDEX_FILE` pointing at it: `git read-tree <checkedSha>`, then `git update-index --refresh` (exit 0 or 1), then `git diff --name-only -z --no-renames`. The checked commit's tree carries no flags.
- Follow the existing temporary-index pattern in src/git/repos.ts (around lines 505–530 and 1235). src/git/hardening.ts already lets `GIT_INDEX_FILE` through.
- Keep the separate `--cached` comparison of the real index against the checked commit.
- Keep failing closed (`trackedClean: false` with a reason) if any step fails.

Tests, with real git: a passing gate that sets `assume-unchanged` and rewrites a tracked file records no evidence; the same with `skip-worktree`; the ordinary rewrite and the untracked/ignored-only cases keep their current results. Each new test fails without the fix. Run only the test files you change plus test/gate-executor.test.ts, `bunx biome check` on changed files and `bunx tsc --noEmit`. Never run the full suite in a factory run.

original.title: Retire the finished worker job before an authentication fallback runs locally
original.detail:
Thank you: the classification is structural and the fallback paths are right. One defect in the new worker path.

When a worker reports an authentication failure, lanAgentExecutor adopts the report (line ~201) and returns `fallback(id)` (line ~217). The completed job stays attached to the run's state (`agentJob`). If that local session then edits files and ends in quota exhaustion, or another authentication failure, `Context.invoke` moves to the next candidate. That candidate reopens the same completed job and tries to adopt it again. The clean-worktree guard in src/pipeline/engine.ts (~line 1268) then stops the run with `Coordinator HEAD or worktree changed during worker session`, so the next provider never runs. Before this PR, a worker authentication error was returned as the round's result, so the intermediate local session didn't exist.

Review reproduced this in test/pipeline-routing.test.ts. Configure workers for implement. Make enqueueAgentJob queue the job, mark it leased and complete it with `{status: "unavailable", failureClass: "authentication", sha: request.parentSha, ...}`. The first provider's local session writes partial.txt and returns status quota; the second succeeds. Expected: the run succeeds and the implementers are [first, second]. Actual: needs_human with the message above.

Fix: before handing execution to the local session, retire that worker job durably, keeping its publication state, so that no later candidate in the same invocation reopens it. Apply the same retirement to the existing confinement-startup fallback, which uses the same `fallback(id)` path. Add the regression test above; it must fail without the fix.

original.title: Document the rollback limit of the new failureClass report field
original.detail:
Older coordinators parse worker result reports strictly and reject unknown keys. A worker on this release that reports `failureClass` to a coordinator rolled back to an earlier release will have that report refused. Release matching prevents new mixed-version leases, but a job already in flight across a rollback can still finish this way. If the worker had already published changes, the old coordinator then needs a human to reconcile the run branch. Reports without the field are unaffected.

No protocol negotiation needed: add one sentence where docs/OPERATIONS.md describes rolling back (or next to the worker protocol in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md). Say that rolling back past this release while a worker job is in flight can reject that job's report if it hit an authentication failure, and that cancelling the run's worker job before rolling back avoids it.

original.title: Reconcile the reader-dependency fixture with #863: a setup that rewrites tracked source now yields no gate evidence
original.detail:
Thank you: the reader-dependency mechanism itself looks right. The post-merge gate failed because of an interaction with #863 ("Gate evidence: record none when a gate changed tracked files"), which landed on main while this ran. After merging origin/main, all 8 new tests fail with the run at needs_human instead of succeeded:
- the 8 `reader dependencies: <harness> <layout>` cases in test/pipeline-reader-dependencies.test.ts;
- `LAN review installs dependencies and acceptance verification stays local` in test/pipeline-lan-agent.test.ts.

The run's error is `Delivery refused: ... missing or inconsistent passing round evidence`, and the run logs `Gate evidence withheld: tracked files changed: ["reader-source.ts"]`.

Cause: `readerDependencyFixture`'s setup command (test/reader-dependencies-support.ts:49) rewrites the tracked file reader-source.ts ("Setup may run package scripts that alter tracked source without moving HEAD"). Since #863, a gate that changes tracked files records no evidence, by design, and delivery requires passing evidence.

Fix: first merge origin/main. Then change the fixture so setup still proves what you meant, that readers see the committed bytes and not setup's side effects, without altering tracked files. For example, have setup write an untracked, gitignored generated file that the probe imports when present, and assert readers don't see it. If you also want to cover a setup that changes tracked source, add a separate case expecting the #863 outcome: no gate evidence and delivery refused. Don't weaken #863's check. Run test/pipeline-reader-dependencies.test.ts, test/pipeline-lan-agent.test.ts and test/pipeline-verification.test.ts on the merged tree, plus `bunx biome check` on changed files and `bunx tsc --noEmit`. Never run the full suite in a factory run.

original.title: Prepare reader dependencies where the reader actually runs, not on the coordinator before routing
original.detail:
Thank you: the fixture fix is right, and the mechanism holds up. Trust comes from the persisted base config, setup runs under runLocalGates confinement with a gate slot, and older workers ignore the new field.

One regression. `prepareReaderCheckout(cwd, gates.setup, ...)` now runs on the coordinator before review routing, whenever `localSetupReady` is false. A run whose gates pass remotely, and whose review is dispatched to a paired worker, therefore runs the setup on the coordinator first. If the toolchain exists only on the worker, the run now fails with `Reader setup failed` before review is dispatched. Before this PR, the same run succeeded.

Review reproduced this in test/pipeline-lan-agent.test.ts, `quick LAN review does not require the worker toolchain on the coordinator`:
- `.limitless.toml` has setup `case "$PWD" in *remote-gate-*|*worker-agent-*) true ;; *) echo "toolchain is available only on the worker" >&2; exit 1 ;; esac` and no checks.
- A fake LAN `GateExecutor` clones the checkout into `remote-gate-<id>` and runs `runLocalGates` there.
- The quick-profile run's review handler throws if review runs locally.
- Expected: the run succeeds with review on the worker. Actual: `Reader setup failed`.

Fix: run the coordinator's setup lazily, only when a reader is about to run locally: local review, local verify, or the LAN executor's local fallback. Keep the worker-side preparation for review jobs, and keep preparing before concurrent local verification. Add that regression test.

original.title: A reader-setup failure should end resumably, attributed to the stage that needed it
original.detail:
When the coordinator's reader setup fails, for example on a transient `bun install` network error, `prepareReaderCheckout` throws a plain Error. The whole run then ends `failed`, and the failure is attributed to the audit stage (stage: audit), though audit passed. A run that had passed its gates is lost to one transient install error and can't be resumed.

original.title: Don't make a model call to check the token: use `claude auth status` with the token, and let the session fail closed
original.detail:
Thank you: passing the token to the capability probe and checkLogin through `subscriptionToken`, with redaction, is right.

The validation step costs too much. With a token configured, `checkLogin` now runs `claude --print "Reply OK." --model haiku ...`, a real model request. It runs before every Claude job on the worker and in the capability probe, which refreshes every 5 minutes (`capabilityRefreshMs ?? 300_000`). That's about 288 extra subscription requests per worker per day, plus one per job, and a few seconds on every job start. That's my fault: the issue said a rejected token must make the check fail.

Change of requirement: with a token configured, run `claude auth status` with `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` in its environment, as you already do for the probe, and treat its result as the login check. No model request. A rejected token is then caught when the session starts. Since #870 that's classified as an authentication failure, the round runs locally, and it never counts as a round. So the check only has to establish that the worker has a usable login configured.

Keep the redaction and the error text when the status command itself fails. Update the tests: a worker with a configured token and no stored login reports logged in and runs a Claude job; no model request is made by the probe or checkLogin; without a token, behaviour is as before. Run the affected test files, `bunx biome check` on changed files and `bunx tsc --noEmit`. Never run the full suite in a factory run.

original.title: Withhold worker text by line, not by dropping the marker rule: the marker rule was covering matcher gaps
original.detail:
Thank you: the change does what #878 asked, and the MCP test is meaningful. But review found that #878's premise was wrong. The `[redacted]`-marker rule wasn't redundant: it was covering three matcher gaps, and disabling it for worker data makes all three leak. Each was reproduced with this PR:

1. **Escaped or split credentials (P1).** A complete credential in JSON-escaped form (`review-token\/synthetic-credential`, with `\/`) isn't decoded by the private matcher (src/gates/private.ts ~150), so it survives intact. A credential split across two lines also survives. Previously the whole field was withheld because a marker appeared somewhere in it.
2. **Truncation (P2).** `privateOutputData` calls `privacy(field)` without `truncated` (private-output.ts ~24, keys at ~27). A clipped credential or private-string prefix at the end of a field survives.
3. **Ordering (P2).** `WorkerStore.sanitize` redacts credentials before checking private strings (workers.ts ~141). A private value with a credential inside it, such as `review-host-<credential>.example`, becomes `review-host-[redacted].example`, no longer matches its private entry, and survives.

Owner decision (2026-10-24): for worker data, withhold by line instead.
- Split every string value from a worker into lines.
- Check each original line, before credential redaction, against the private-strings entries and the registered credentials.
- A line that matches, or that already contains the literal `[redacted]`, is replaced by `[withheld: private text; 1 line]`.
- All other lines are kept, with `redactCredentials` applied as a final pass.
- Check the last line of each value as possibly truncated (`truncated: true`), so a clipped fragment there is withheld.
- Object keys keep today's whole-key withholding.
- An unreadable policy still withholds everything.
- MCP results and digests keep today's whole-field behaviour.
- Use one implementation: a line mode of the existing privacy filter, not a second filter.

Tests:
- A worker failure excerpt with an assertion line, expected/received lines and a stack keeps those lines when another line contains `[redacted]`. Only that line is withheld.
- Each of the three reproductions above stays withheld at least at the line level: the escaped credential's line (it contains the marker in the reproduction; add a case where it doesn't, and record what happens), the truncated final line, and the private value containing a credential.
- MCP still withholds whole fields that contain `[redacted]`.
- Each test fails without the change.

Run only test/workers.test.ts, test/mcp-proxy.test.ts and test/digest-cli.test.ts, plus `bunx biome check` on changed files and `bunx tsc --noEmit`. Never run the full suite in a factory run.

original.title: Publish only fixed lifecycle text, never run.error, and check the exact body that is posted
original.detail:
Thank you: the reconciliation design, label mapping, App identity wiring and failure isolation are right. The queue is live on this repository, so the following must hold before these writes reach real issues.

`needs_human` and `failed` comments embed `run.error`. That text is internal: review reproduced a failed run's worktree and data-directory paths (`/Users/<user>/...`, `/private/var/...`) appearing verbatim in the outgoing body, because no private-strings entry matched and `sanitizePublication` is never applied. Separately, when the check rejects a body, the fallback is posted unchecked (P3). Reproduced: with the run id listed as private, the fallback published it.

Change of requirement (orchestrator, 2026-10-24): lifecycle comments carry only fixed text per event, the run id and the run link, for example `Limitless run <id> needs you: see <run link>.` No `run.error` or other free-form run text.

Pass the exact body through `redactCredentials`, then the same publication path PR reports use (`sanitizePublication` with the worktree and home), then the private-strings check. If the check still rejects it, post nothing for that event: record it done and log the reason. Never post a fallback that wasn't checked.

Tests:
- a failed run whose error contains a worktree path, a home path, a credential and a private string posts none of them;
- a body rejected by the private-strings check isn't posted at all.

original.title: Record every observed event before delivering any, so a failed POST can't lose a later event
original.detail: Events are derived from the run's current status (~line 99), and the comment loop `break`s on the first failed POST (~line 165) before later events are recorded. Reproduced: the start comment fails while the run needs a human; the run resolves before the next poll; the needs-you event is never posted. Fix: when a status is first observed, record its event as pending (with its fixed body) in the effects table, then deliver pending events in order. A failed POST stops this issue's delivery for this poll, but every observed event stays pending until it's delivered. Test that exact sequence.

original.title: The legacy migration must suppress historical comments only, not future transitions of runs active at deploy
original.detail: The migration marks every existing run `legacy`, `issueLifecycleRuns()` excludes legacy runs forever, and the notifier suppresses their comments. So a run that's running during the deploy and fails afterwards gets neither its failed label nor its comment. Reproduced across a database reopen. Test: a run created before the migration that fails afterwards gets the failed label and exactly one failed comment, and no started comment.

original.title: Re-approval after failure: a currently present priority label, applied after the failure, in timeline order
original.detail:
Two problems in the failed-then-re-approved check.

1. It searches all historical priority applications, so a trusted priority label applied after the failure and then removed still re-approves. Reproduced.
2. It compares timestamps with a strict `>`, so a re-approval in the same second as the failure label stays blocked. Reproduced.

Fix: re-approval requires a priority label that is present now and whose latest trusted application comes after the latest `limitless:failed` application in timeline order (the timeline's sequence, not timestamps). Test both cases, plus a failure label applied by an untrusted account.

original.title: Bound the per-poll lifecycle work
original.detail:
`issueLifecycleRuns()` loads every non-legacy run, with its full `state_json`, on every poll, and reconciliation then does several reads per run. Review measured 50 run reads and 150 effect reads per unchanged poll with 25 completed runs, and that grows forever. It also runs before queue admission, so many runs with outstanding writes delay admission.

Fix: select only runs that still have work: a non-final status, a label cursor that differs from the desired label, or a pending effect. Cap GitHub calls per poll, resuming the rest next poll. Test that a poll over many completed runs makes no GitHub calls and a bounded number of reads.

original.title: Regression tests for A–E (from review): add them
Tie re-approval to the latest failure episode, judged only by timeline order
original.detail:
Thank you: A, B and E are fixed, and review confirmed both migrations apply in order and match a single correct migration on populated databases. This is the last review round.

The re-approval guard compares the failure label's timestamp with the latest run's completion time. Suppose a retry is created after reconciliation and fails before the next poll. The previous run's `limitless:failed` label is still present, and the lifecycle (~src/integrations/issue-lifecycle.ts:196) doesn't re-apply it. If that label predates the latest failure's second, every later trusted approval is rejected forever. If both failures fall in the same second, rounding lets the earlier approval authorize another retry with no fresh approval. Both reproduced.

Fix:
- When a run fails, make the failure a new labeled event even if the label is already present (remove it, then add it), and record which run that event belongs to.
- Eligibility then uses only timeline order: re-approval needs a trusted priority label, present now, applied after the most recent `limitless:failed` labeled event. Drop the completion-time comparison.

Test both reproduced cases.

Behind 49 persistently failing calls, a task that needs two calls (an owner-comment check, or a label re-read plus write) gets only the last slot. The next poll starts after it and repeats the same pattern, so it starves indefinitely. Reproduced for labels and comments over ten polls while respecting the 50-call cap.

Fix: before starting a task, check that the remaining budget covers the calls it needs. If it doesn't, end the poll with the cursor on that task, so it runs first next poll with the full budget. A task that fails rotates to the back, as now.

original.detail:

original.title: Keep the confirmation tests eligible after #897, and prove a compound check is refused
Check private strings once, decoded, on complete text before any credential redaction or cut
original.detail:
Thank you: review confirmed that complete MCP values and worker fields are now checked before credential redaction, and that all 11 added tests fail on main. Three remaining defects share one cause: the authoritative decoded private matcher doesn't run on the complete text before credential redaction and before every cut.

1. **Unicode escapes defeat the ordering.** Gate capture (~src/gates/run.ts:152, `privateLiteralStream`) uses literal matching. Take the private value `host-synthetic/overlap-token-909.private-domain-909.example`, an overlapping registered credential `prefix-host-synthetic/overlap-token-909`, and output that writes the dots as `\u002e`. Capture produces `[redacted]\u002eprivate-domain-909\u002eexample`, and the later private matcher finds nothing. A real local-gate probe found that remainder in the stored event and in the dispatched model prompt.
2. **Cuts lose provenance.** Failure excerpts clip diagnostics and append an identity with no clipping metadata (~src/gates/failures.ts:51, ~run.ts:171, ~src/util/private-output.ts:28). One reproduction kept `protected-host-9` from `protected-host-909.example`, and every privacy callback received `truncated=false`. An encoded host clipped by the 6,000-character gate tail kept `rivate-domain-909\u002eexample`, and `WorkerStore.sanitize` also returned that fragment.
3. **Length is used as provenance.** A complete 4,000-character message, `"!".repeat(3999) + "h"`, is withheld when a private entry starts with `h`, though nothing was clipped (~private-output.ts:31). The 200/500-code-point feed heuristics have the same ambiguity.

Fix: at each capture boundary (gate streams and diagnostics, failure excerpts, the gate tail, worker data, MCP results and errors, prompts), run the authoritative private check, with its decoded forms, on the complete text before credential redaction and before any cut. Carry truncation as an explicit flag from the place that actually cut, never inferred from length. Keep one implementation. Add one regression per case above, using these inputs.

original.title: Replace the backtracking regex in the private matcher with a linear scan
original.detail: CodeQL `js/redos` is real. The nested repetition allows exponentially many partitions of consecutive backslashes when the suffix fails. Worst-case family: `privateMatches("diagnostic " + "\\".repeat(n) + "!", [{ value: "protected-host.example", entry: 1 }], true)`. Measured on this PR: 12 backslashes 0.71 ms, 18 12.3 ms, 22 179 ms, 26 2,224 ms. That synchronously stalls the daemon. The regex exists on main too, and this PR adds callers through truncation handling. Replace it with a linear suffix scan. Add a regression on that input family with n = 64 that asserts the result; leave timing to the benchmark, as test/AGENTS.md asks. Confirm the CodeQL alert clears.

original.title: Keep redaction linear on escaped JSON, and report before-and-after timings
original.detail:
This is the hot path (AGENTS.md: 'Hot paths are measured at production size'). On 5 MiB of realistic logs and JSON with occasional `\/`, eight private entries, median total ms / worst stall ms:
- credentials at 50/200/600 registered: main 18.5/18.2/18.2, PR 35.4/37.3/35.2;
- private matching at 0–600 credentials: main ~1,300 ms, PR ~2,550–2,620 ms.

Without escaped slashes, the PR matches main. Cause: credential matching builds offsets for the entire string after the first escaped slash (~credential-matcher.ts:118), and private normalization does another whole-text decoding pass (~src/gates/private.ts:155). Fix: decode and map offsets only around escape sequences, in a single pass shared by both matchers, and keep the plain-text path unchanged. Put one before-and-after table in the PR, using scripts/benchmark-credential-redaction.ts extended with an escaped-JSON workload.

The PR is already far over the issue's ~40-line budget. Keep this round to what these four findings need, reuse existing helpers, and report the source line count.

original.title: Apply the workflow guard in scripts/land-pr.sh before it pushes
Make a recorded post-merge rejection stop the previous engine too
original.detail:
Thank you: review confirmed that with this PR's engine, all six restart windows keep the reason without merging or gating again. That covers before and after the rejection record, after the reset, after `clean`, after the state save and after the status write. Worker attribution and the coordinator excerpt from #891 survive in the reason, and both new tests fail on the previous engine.

**P2: a daemon downgrade can retry a durably rejected attempt. Reproduced.** The rejection checkpoint saves only the new `postMergeRejection` field (~src/pipeline/engine.ts:3471). After the rollback's state save (~3251), `needsHumanReason` is still unset; it's saved later (~449). Interrupt this engine after that save, then resume the same database with the `origin/main` engine. It ignores `postMergeRejection`, merges and gates again, and returns `succeeded` when the next gate passes. Worker executions went from 2 to 3, `error` became null, and the rejection stayed recorded but unenforced. AGENTS.md requires the previous release to keep working after a rollback, and a passing retry must never hide the original failure.

Fix: at every point after the rejection is recorded, the state must also stop the previous engine. One way: in the same save as the rejection record, set what the previous engine already honours on resume, the run's `needs_human` status and reason. Then make this engine's rollback steps idempotent cleanup that never depends on resuming. Verify it as review did: for each restart window, resume with the previous engine as well as this one. It must end `needs_human` with the original reason and no new merge or gate execution. A test can load the previous behaviour by clearing the new field before resuming; say what it proves.

Run only test/pipeline-delivery-restart.test.ts and test/pipeline-gates.test.ts, plus `bunx biome check` on changed files and `bunx tsc --noEmit`. Never run the full suite in a factory run.

original.title: Don't let the rollback's final status writes overwrite a resolution recorded meanwhile
original.detail:
Thank you: review confirmed the round. All 12 restart cases pass with both this engine and the real `origin/main` engine, in every window from before the record to after the final status write. Each ends `needs_human` with the original reason, with no new merge or gate execution. The `merging` change keeps every non-rejection resume path correct, and the new branches are reachable only for rejections.

**P2: early terminal publication lets the rollback overwrite a human resolution. Reproduced.** The run is published as `needs_human` (~src/pipeline/engine.ts:3503) before the rollback is awaited. original.title: Take the enable boundary from GitHub's clock at enable time, not from issue activity
original.detail: The boundary is the newest `updatedAt`/`createdAt` among open issues. This is #900's recipe, and the recipe is wrong. Review reproduced both cases. (1) With quiet open issues last updated months ago, reopening a closed issue that holds an old trusted command (created before enabling, after that old timestamp) runs it. (2) With no open issues at the first poll, no boundary is saved; the first later command then sets a boundary equal to its own time and never runs. Fix: on a poll with no stored boundary, before the issue list query, read GitHub's current time from the `Date` response header of `GET /rate_limit` (`gh api --include rate_limit`, which doesn't count against the limit), store it, and process nothing in that poll. If the header is missing or unparsable, store nothing and retry next poll. Tests: both reproductions, plus a command posted after enabling on a repository that had zero open issues runs exactly once.

original.title: Never run comment commands from bot logins; don't depend on the identity lookup to exclude the factory
original.detail: When the identity lookup fails, `bot` is null, so the factory-bot exclusion is off. `[github.queue] trusted` accepts `[bot]` logins (config.ts), so an App bot listed as trusted then gets its own `/limitless` comment run (review reproduced it with an injected identity failure). The trusted author is also stored as `requestedBy`, and `requestedBy === "dependabot[bot]"` changes routing and review (context.ts ~360, engine.ts ~1984). Simplest fix: a comment command needs a trusted login without the `[bot]` suffix, whatever the identity lookup returns. Keep the lookup only for parsing the `@<bot>` mention form, and skip mention-form comments (without recording them) when it fails. Tests: a trusted `[bot]` author's command never runs, with and without an identity failure; a mention-form command waits for a later poll when the lookup fails, then runs once.

original.title: Bound hinted polls when polls fail
original.detail: `pollNow` cancels the regular delay after every completed tick, and `notBefore` is set only from successfully parsed rate-limit data. Say where complete-text checks run, and bound the daemon's event-loop stall
original.detail:
Thank you: the inventory, the provenance contract (true / false / unknown, with no length heuristics), the cut-then-recheck rule with the NFKC combining-mark example, and the five dependency-ordered c2 slices are what #919 needs.

One gap. The cost section budgets one to three complete checks of 5 MiB per gate, estimated at 1.3 to 3.9 s of CPU, but it doesn't say where that work runs. Run synchronously in the daemon, each check is an event-loop stall of that length. AGENTS.md's hot-path rule asks for the worst stall, and the daemon already logs stalls over its threshold. Add to the design:
(1) Where complete-text checks run: for example a worker thread per check, or bounded synchronous slices with yields between them. Name the choice and why.
(2) A stall budget, such as no single synchronous slice over 50 ms on the daemon thread for any input size.
(3) Make the c2.2 benchmark report the worst event-loop stall beside the medians, and add it to the c2.1/c2.2 acceptance.
Also update the baseline: since #921, and with #923 (`\/` decoding plus layer caching) about to land, `privateMatches` on 5 MiB with eight entries measured about 110 to 260 ms here (scripts/benchmark-credential-redaction.ts), against the 1.3 s figure quoted from the issue. Keep the 1.3 s as the issue's figure, but plan from the measured one. State that "supported" means whatever `normalizedLayers` does at c2's base, including #917's `\/` decoding once it lands.

original.title: Bind the criterion to the named testcase in the run's own JUnit report; drop the name-filter option parsing
original.detail:
The run looped five rounds on one cause. `coveringTestRefusal` accepts file-level evidence: `summary.passed >= 1`, the file in `passedFiles`, and a token heuristic over skip identities. So any option that changes which test runs, such as `-tunrelated` or `'-t' unrelated` in the template, lets an unrelated passing test in the same file satisfy the criterion. Each round rejected one more spelling of the option, and review found the next. Fixing it by parsing shell options can't converge.

Fix it at the evidence instead:
(1) The covering run writes a JUnit report to a fresh, factory-chosen path. Gates already set `LIMITLESS_GATE_REPORT`; add Bun's `--reporter=junit --reporter-outfile=<that path>` as factory-built argv after the template's arguments.
(2) Parse it with the existing JUnit reader (src/gates/junit.ts).
(3) Accept only when the report contains a testcase whose file is the requested file and whose full name equals the requested name, with no failure, error or skipped child, and the run left tracked files unchanged.
If the report is missing, stale (it existed before the run, or is older than the run's start) or unparseable, refuse. If the template overrides the reporter or the name filter, the named testcase is simply absent and the run is refused: fail closed, with no parsing.

Remove the option-parsing check (~85), `skipMatches`/`matchingSkips` and the summary or passedFiles conditions. Keep passing the name as a literal, regex-escaped filter so the run stays targeted, but correctness must no longer depend on it.

Tests, each failing without the change:
- a template containing `-tunrelated`, `'-t' unrelated` or `--test-name-pattern=unrelated`, with the requested title absent from the file, is refused;
- the requested title present and passing is accepted;
- skipped, failed and missing-report cases are refused;
- a report left over from an earlier run at the same path is refused.

The issue's budget was about 120 source lines and this PR has about 394. Removing the parsing should bring it down; name any remaining overrun in the report.

original.detail: Linux CI fails the six 'covering JUnit requires fresh exact testcase evidence' cases. `mtimeMs < startedAt` compares filesystem time with `Date.now()` (run.ts ~163), and on Linux a just-written report's mtime can lag the wall clock. original.title: Share the repository-tree load between concurrent callers with different abort signals
original.detail:

original.title: Keep the configured repository spelling: lowercasing it makes the queue create a duplicate repository record
original.detail:
`loadConfig` now stores `github.queue.repos` lowercased. The queue then passes that name to `issueRunRequest` and `factory.createRun` (src/integrations/issue-queue.ts ~434 and ~359).

`createRun` resolves the repository with `resolveRepo` (src/git/repos.ts), which calls `store.getRepoBySlug`, and that matches `slug = ?` case-sensitively (`repos.slug` is `TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE`, no NOCASE). With the usual configuration `repos = ["MattFlower/limitless"]` and the existing row `MattFlower/limitless`, the lookup for `mattflower/limitless` finds nothing (checked against a copy of a real store: 0 rows). `resolveRepo` would then run `gh repo view` and `upsertRepo` a second repository row with its own id, cache, merge policy and run history. Every queue-created run would land on it.

#977 asked to canonicalize repository **keys** and to deduplicate configured names case-insensitively; it didn't ask to change the name the queue acts on. Fix:
- Keep each configured name as written.
- Deduplicate case-insensitively at load, keeping the first spelling.
- Lowercase only the keys of `snapshots`, `invalidated` and similar maps.
- Pass the configured name (or the stored repository's slug) to GraphQL, `issueRunRequest` and `createRun`.

Test: with `repos = ["Owner/Repo", "owner/repo"]` and a stored repository `Owner/Repo`:
- config yields exactly `["Owner/Repo"]`;
- a queue admission's `createRun` request uses `Owner/Repo`;
- the store still holds one repository row.
Show that the test fails with the current lowercasing.

original.title: Don't scan every run's prompt on each poll to seed the comparison
original.detail:
`issueRunObservations()` runs at the start of every poll. It selects every run with its `prompt` and parses `source_ref`, and the queue then calls `linkedIssues` on each row. On a copy of a real store (732 runs, 3.0 MB of prompts) that is 36–38 ms of synchronous work per poll: query about 25 ms, `linkedIssues` about 10 ms. #976 brought the whole poll down to 26 ms, so this more than doubles the event-loop block, and it grows with every run ever created. AGENTS.md: "Hot paths are measured at production size."

The decision only needs runs that can change an issue's admission, so compare against what the poll already holds. Invalidate an issue key when a published run:
- is the snapshot's latest run, or its owner, for that key and its `status`, `finishedAt` or linkage differs from the snapshot; or
- is linked to that key (via `linkedIssues(msg.run)`) but isn't the snapshot's latest run for it, which covers a new or different run.
An accounting-only publication of a completed run (`refreshRunTotals`) then changes nothing, which is #977's second case. Before a repository's snapshot exists, keep #976's behavior for that repository.

Report one before-and-after timing in the PR, using `scripts/benchmark-issue-queue.ts` or a copy of a real store at a few thousand runs. Keep #977's two regressions, and add one showing that an accounting-only publication during the poll doesn't defer admission.

`handles` starts empty (~49) and is filled only by this instance's successful writes. Recovery restores SQLite ownership without registering handles (~239). So `start({ active: () => true, … })` never renews an existing confirmed lease, or one whose acquisition recovery confirmed, and the lease expires unless the caller reacquires it. That misses the requirement to renew every active confirmed held handle. Reproduced for both restart cases: zero renewal writes on the tick.
Rebuild the renewable handle set from the store on construction and after recovery.

original.title: Reconcile a pending never-confirmed acquisition before deciding another run's acquisition
original.detail:
A's first acquisition ends `unconfirmed` without applying. When GitHub becomes readable and shows the ref still absent, B's acquisition returns `refused` at once (~107), before reconciliation can drop A's intent and forget its never-confirmed row. Invariant 8 requires reconciliation before each operation. Reproduced: expected B to acquire generation 1, got `refused`.
Reconcile the pending intent first, then decide B's result.

original.title: One CommonMark fence tracker for both scanners; the section scanner must not toggle on any marker
original.detail:
Round 2's resolution review reproduced this: `section()` flips a boolean on every backtick or tilde marker, so a backtick line inside a tilde fence ends the fence early, a heading inside it becomes a section boundary, and later requirements are silently dropped.

Fences inside the referenced section already refuse under the rule above. Fences elsewhere in the parent are allowed, so the heading scan over the whole parent still has to skip them correctly. Use one helper for both `section()` and `markdownUnits()`: a fence opens on three or more backticks or tildes (at most three leading spaces) and closes only on a line of the same character, at least as long, with nothing after it but spaces. An unclosed fence in the parent refuses "unresolvable source". Remove the separate toggles.

Tests: the reviewer's command as a regression (the referenced section contains the tilde fence, so it refuses with the unsupported-Markdown reason), and a parent whose `## Goal` section is clean but which has a mixed-marker fence *before* `## Goal` containing `## Goal`: it resolves to Goal's units, not ambiguous, and not truncated.
